  In the long wave $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,
  $\chi=U+O(U^{3})$, viscosity drops out, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
  This is the solution of Colleagues 1,4,8 in both rounds, and the core of
  Colleagues 2,5,7.

* $W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, impermeable base variant.  Imposing in addition
  vanishing vertical velocity at the base gives the familiar channel transfer
  $\chi_{2}(kh)=kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]
            =[ \sinh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$,
  which is the $W(h)=0$ version quoted by Colleagues 2,5,6 and the
  lubrication form $\chi_{L}=kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$.
  It coincides with the free-base form to $O(kh)$: 
  $\chi_{2}=kh+O((kh)^{3})$.

The statement of the problem gives $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and prescribes basal
shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, with $u_{x}(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, but does not impose $w(h)=0$.  Hence the
free vertical basal flow solution $\chi=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ is the
one consistent with the stated conditions.  The $W(h)=0$ form is a common
geophysical approximation and is often quoted as the “lubrication’’ limit;
both give $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, so the long-wave thin-plate
estimate $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,
is robust and viscosity independent.

Current best estimate: exact steady Stokes transfer with free base
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,
and the geophysically used long-wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$.
With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification this is the
$e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling quoted in the literature; the
$kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ form is the equivalent $W(h)=0$ impermeable-base
normalisation, identical to $O(kh)$.  Sign convention is a matter of the
definition of $S_{0}$.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes harmonic problem with stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$. Rigid free lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ in steady state. With $\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$ and $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$ the top condition $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives $\rho g e =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. The base conditions used in the statement are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$. No $u_z(h)=0$ is imposed; the base is permeable.

Up to constants $\Phi(z)=A z\sinh kz+B\big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\big]$. Then $B=\rho g e/2\mu k$ from the lid, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=kh A\cosh kh$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives $S_{0}=2\mu k[A\cosh kh+khA\sinh kh+kh B\cosh kh]$. Eliminating $A,B$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$ ,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$ with, up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification,

$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady balance. Long wave $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U\simeq1$,

$\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar thin-plate scaling $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with shape factor $kh$.

If the density in the free-surface condition is kept as $\rho$, the strict conversion to $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$: $\chi_{\rho/\Delta}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$; with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the form quoted above.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant gives $\chi_{a}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=U\,\sech U/[1+U\tanh U]$, which coincides with the permeable-base $\chi$ to $O(U)$: $\chi_{a}=U+O(U^{3})$, $\chi_{a}\sim2U e^{-U}$ for $U\gg1$. Current round colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 all recover the permeable-base result $\chi=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and note the $U\ll1$ limit $\chi\simeq U$. Sign conventions differ but magnitude is as above. ∎

7.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream-function/biharmonic formulation is now stable across the round.
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ from the rigid no-slip lid $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$.
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, $\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Top normal stress: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, i.e. $\Delta\rho g e=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ with $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-dk^{-1}z\sinh kz$
gives $P(z)=2\mu[-kc\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$ and $\Phi'''(z)-k^{2}\Phi'(z)=2k^{2}c\cosh kz-2k d\sinh kz$.

Base conditions used in the stated problem are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ with $u_z$ free at the base.  
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Rightarrow P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\Rightarrow\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
These give
$(c+dh)\cosh kh =k c h\sinh kh$, 
$d=c\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$,
$2\mu c\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]/\big(h\cosh kh\big)=S_{0}$,
hence
$c= S_{0}h\cosh kh/\big\{2\mu\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]\big\}$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k c$ and
$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{A}(kh)$,
$\displaystyle\chi_{A}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
       =\Big[\,U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\Big]^{-1}$,
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$, viscosity independent in steady state.

Long wave $U\ll1$:
$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$, $\chi_{A}=U+O(U^{3})$,
$e_{s}\simeq U S_{0}/\Delta\rho g =kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the quoted thin-plate dynamic topography $e_{s}\approx(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $W(h)=0\iff \Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant used by several colleagues gives the commonly quoted lubrication transfer
$\chi_{B}(U)=U/\big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\big]=1/\big[\sinh U+\cosh U/U\big]$,
$\chi_{B}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and $\chi_{B}\sim U\operatorname{sech}U$ for $U\gg1$.
$\chi_{A}$ and $\chi_{B}$ coincide to $O(U)$; the difference is the $O(1)$ $W(h)=0$ vs free vertical motion at the base. Both give the universal thin-plate limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling. Sign conventions differ by an overall sign.

Unresolved/note: exact normalisation $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$. With the buoyant restoring stress the conventional form is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ above, i.e. $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$. This is the steady viscous topographic response normally quoted.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The current round confirms the stream-function analysis of round 1. With
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, the rigid impermeable lid is
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ in the steady state.  Up to rigid-body motion
$\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Cz\sinh kz$,
$ \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$ and

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

The free lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$,
i.e. $\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}A$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

At the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ is $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_0$.
With $u=kh$,

$A\big( u\sinh u-\cosh u\big)=Ch\cosh u$,

$-2\mu kA\,(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)/(h\cosh u)=S_{0}$,
whence

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(u)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$\displaystyle\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}$,
$u=kh$, independent of $\mu$.  

For $u\ll1$, $\cosh u=1+O(u^{2})$,
$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ and

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

the usual long-wave viscous dynamic-topography scaling.  The
$kh/(\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh)$ family quoted by Colleagues 2,5,6 is the
$W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, impermeable-base variant
$\chi_{L}=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ which coincides with $\chi$ to $O(u)$.
Colleague 7’s $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u+u^{2}/2]$ is the $O(kW)$ correction
to the basal shear condition.  Sign conventions differ by an overall
minus sign.  The essential physics is the $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling
with shape factor $\sim kh$, viscosity dropping out of the steady
balance, and the exact Stokes transfer function above is the one
required by $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$. ∎

reflection_text.8:
The deliberation has now converged on the rigid–impermeable lid stream-function solution with the steady kinematic lid $u_{x}(0)=0$, $u_{z}(0)=\dot e=0\Rightarrow\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in the steady state.  
With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$ and

$\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}\!\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,

the rigid lid gives $\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$.  
Hence $P(0)=-\rho g e$ and with the biharmonic form $P(0)=2\mu k(B+D)$,
$\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k c$ in the canonical parametrisation
$\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-d k^{-1}z\sinh kz$.

Base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ give
$(c+d h)\cosh kh=k c h\sinh kh$ and
$2\mu\big[c h k^{2}\cosh kh-d\cosh kh-d h k\sinh kh\big]=S_{0}$,
i.e. $d=c\big[k\sinh kh/\cosh kh-1/h\big]$ and

$c= S_{0}h\cosh kh/\big\{2\mu\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]\big\}$.

Thus in the $\rho$ normalisation

$e_{s}=2\mu k c/\rho g
      =S_{0}/\rho g\; \chi_{\rho}(U)$,
$\chi_{\rho}(U)=U\cosh U/\big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big]$,
$U=kh$,

$\chi_{\rho}= \big[U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\big]^{-1}$,
independent of $\mu$. With the buoyant restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ the conventional form is
$e_{s}= \chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi_{\rho}\to\chi$ up to the
trivial $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement. Often written

$\chi(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}}
       =\dfrac{1}{U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U}$.

Long wave $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$ :

$\cosh U\simeq1$,
$\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

which is the quoted thin-plate viscous dynamic-topography scaling,
$k h\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. The viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

The $W(h)=0$ / impermeable base, $kW$–neglected lubrication family
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=U\,{\rm sech}U/[1+U\tanh U]$,
i.e. $\chi_{L}^{-1}=\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U$, is now recognised as the
$A\neq0$/$W(h)=0$ variant. It coincides with the exact $\chi_{\rho}$
to $O(U)$ and shares the same $U\ll1$ limit $\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$.
Colleague 7’s $\chi_{7}=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U+U^{2}/2]$ is the $kW$
correction to the basal shear boundary condition and also tends to
$U$ for $U\ll1$.

Sign is conventional; the magnitude is as above. The disagreement in
round 0 between the $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ family and the $W'(0)=0$ only
family is resolved in round 1 in favour of the $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
i.e. $u_{z}(0)=u_{x}(0)=0$ steady lid, giving the above exact transfer
function, whose thin-plate limit is the familiar $e_{s}\approx kh\,
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi\simeq kh$.
reflection_text.2:
The deliberation has converged on the Stokes stream-function solution.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$ and the rigid impermeable lid
$\Phi(0)=0,\;\Phi'(0)=0$.  Then
$\sigma_{zz}= -[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.

On the lid $u_x(0)=0$ is $\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. with the usual buoyant
restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, so that $P(0)=-\Delta\rho g e$.

At the base the stated conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$.  No $u_z(h)=0$ is imposed.  With
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $C=-A$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,
the two base conditions together with $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ give

$A=-\Delta\rho g e/4\mu k^{2}$, $B+D=-2kA$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\;\Leftrightarrow\;A(e^{a}+e^{-a})+h(Be^{a}-De^{-a})=0$, $a=kh$,

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\;\Leftrightarrow\;
S_{0}=2\mu\big[e^{a}(k^{2}A+kB(1+a))+e^{-a}(-k^{2}A-kD(1-a))\big]$.

Eliminating $B,D$ yields the exact steady transfer

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{\rm ex}(kh)$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\,U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\,\Big]^{-1},\quad U=kh$,

independent of $\mu$.  With the $\rho$ normalisation used in the
$\sigma_{zz}$ condition this is
$\chi_{\rho}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and $e_{s}=
\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$, the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement giving the
form quoted in the question.

In particular
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$.
In the geophysically relevant long-wave thin-plate limit
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$, $\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

the viscosity dropping out of the steady balance.  This is the
$U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ form obtained by Colleagues 1,4,8 and
summarised by Colleagues 2,3,5,6,7.

The $kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ family
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=
[\sinh U+\cosh U/U]^{-1}$ is the conventional lubrication / viscous-
channel form obtained if the extra kinematic condition $W(h)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$, is imposed at the base.  It satisfies
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$
to $O(U)$; it is the form most often quoted in the literature.
The problem as stated imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not $W(h)=0$,
so the exact Stokes solution is $\chi_{\rm ex}$ above, which reduces to
the familiar $\chi\approx kh$ in the long-wave limit.  Sign is a
convention, $e_{s}\propto \pm S_{0}$.
reflection_text.3:
The linear Stokes problem with stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$. Rigid free lid $u_x(0)=0$ in steady state is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ with $\sigma_{zz}=-(P+2\mu k\Phi')\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi')$. Hence $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)$ and $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

Base conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi](h)=S_0$. With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$.

The two base conditions give
$(A+Bh)e^{kh}=(-A+Dh)e^{-kh}$ and the shear condition fixes $A,B$ up to $S_0/\mu$. Elimination gives
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and
$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=2\mu A[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[kh\cosh kh]$.
With $\rho g e_s=(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)$ one obtains the viscosity-independent steady transfer

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi(kh)=\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
       =\Big[\dfrac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\dfrac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$.

The viscosity drops out of the steady balance. For $U=kh\ll1$,
$\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})$ and
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
This is the $U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ family quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8.

The alternative lubrication / impermeable base family
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=1/[\sinh U+\cosh U/U]$ follows from the extra kinematic condition $\Phi(h)=0$, i.e. $W(h)=0$, $u_z(h)=0$. It coincides with the exact $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ solution to $O(U)$ and gives the same long-wave limit $\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$. The present statement uses only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ at the base, so the exact steady factor is the $kh\cosh kh/[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]$ form, reducing to $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$. Sign is conventional; $e_{s}>0$ for $S_{0}>0$ with the chosen orientation. The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification is the usual buoyant normalisation.
reflection_text.1:
The linear Stokes problem can be written with a stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=-(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.
With the rigid lid $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ the biharmonic solution is
$\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz e^{kz}+d z e^{-kz}$ with $d=-2ka-b$. Then

$\sigma_{zz}=[-p-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,

$p(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$, $b+d=-2ka$ so that on the free lid
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-p(0)=\rho g e$, i.e. $\rho g e=4\mu k^{2}a$.

At the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff p(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ and the prescribed
basal shear $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$ i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.
With $U=kh$ this gives

$a k[\cosh U+U e^{-U}]+U b\cosh U=0$,

$a k[\cosh U-U e^{-U}]+b[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=S_{0}/4\mu k$,

whence

$b=\dfrac{S_{0}}{4\mu k}\dfrac{\cosh U+U e^{-U}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}},\qquad
a=-\dfrac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^{2}}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}}$,

and

$e_{s}= \dfrac{2\mu k}{\rho g}(b+d)=\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,$

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(U)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{\rho}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}$,

and with the conventional identification $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,
$\chi(U)=\rho\Delta\rho^{-1}U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$.  The viscosity
drops out of the steady balance.  In particular

$\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi(U)\sim2Ue^{-U}$ for $U\gg1$,

so that the long-wave thin-plate limit is

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

the familiar $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic topography scaling.

The $U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=U\,[\cosh U+U\sinh U]^{-1}$ family obtained by
Colleagues 2,5,6,7 is the $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable base variant.
With the stated boundary conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$u_{x}(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ no vertical velocity condition is
imposed at the base, so $\Phi(h)=0$ is not required.  The $W(h)=0$ form

$\chi_{B}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi_{B}=U+O(U^{3})$, coincides with the exact transfer
$\chi_{\rho}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ to $O(U)$ and is the
lubrication/channel form most often quoted in the geophysical literature.
Colleagues 1,4,8 give the exact $U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ form; the
disagreement is only the conventional $W(h)=0$ normalisation.  Up to the
trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ identification this is the steady
viscous response $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the $kh$ long-wave
limit quoted above.
reflection_text.4:
The round-1 public set is a repetition of the round-0 set with essentially the same two families.

* Stream-function family with the rigid impermeable lid $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,
  $p=-\mu k^{-1}(\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi')$, 
  $\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
  $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$.  With the stated base conditions
  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$,
  the solution can be written with
  $\Phi=A\sinh kz+Bz\sinh kz-Akz\cosh kz$, $P(0)=-2\mu k^{2}A=-\rho g e$, 
  $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
  Elimination gives $A=-\rho ge/2\mu k^{2}$,
  $B=-A[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/h\cosh kh$ and
  $-2\mu kA[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]/h\cosh kh=S_{0}$.
  Hence
  $e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$, i.e. with the buoyant
  restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$
  $e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
  $\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]
          =[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$.
  In the long wave $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,
  $\chi=U+O(U^{3})$, viscosity drops out, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
  This is the solution of Colleagues 1,4,8 in both rounds, and the core of
  Colleagues 2,5,7.

* $W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, impermeable base variant.  Imposing in addition
  vanishing vertical velocity at the base gives the familiar channel transfer
  $\chi_{2}(kh)=kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]
            =[ \sinh kh+\cosh kh/kh]^{-1}$,
  which is the $W(h)=0$ version quoted by Colleagues 2,5,6 and the
  lubrication form $\chi_{L}=kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$.
  It coincides with the free-base form to $O(kh)$: 
  $\chi_{2}=kh+O((kh)^{3})$.

The statement of the problem gives $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and prescribes basal
shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, with $u_{x}(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, but does not impose $w(h)=0$.  Hence the
free vertical basal flow solution $\chi=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ is the
one consistent with the stated conditions.  The $W(h)=0$ form is a common
geophysical approximation and is often quoted as the “lubrication’’ limit;
both give $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$, so the long-wave thin-plate
estimate $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,
is robust and viscosity independent.

Current best estimate: exact steady Stokes transfer with free base
$e_{s}= \chi(kh)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}]$,
and the geophysically used long-wave limit $\chi\simeq kh$.
With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification this is the
$e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling quoted in the literature; the
$kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ form is the equivalent $W(h)=0$ impermeable-base
normalisation, identical to $O(kh)$.  Sign convention is a matter of the
definition of $S_{0}$.
reflection_text.6:
The Stokes harmonic problem with stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$. Rigid free lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ in steady state. With $\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$ and $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$ the top condition $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives $\rho g e =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. The base conditions used in the statement are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$. No $u_z(h)=0$ is imposed; the base is permeable.

Up to constants $\Phi(z)=A z\sinh kz+B\big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\big]$. Then $B=\rho g e/2\mu k$ from the lid, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=kh A\cosh kh$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives $S_{0}=2\mu k[A\cosh kh+khA\sinh kh+kh B\cosh kh]$. Eliminating $A,B$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$ ,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$ with, up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification,

$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady balance. Long wave $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U\simeq1$,

$\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar thin-plate scaling $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with shape factor $kh$.

If the density in the free-surface condition is kept as $\rho$, the strict conversion to $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$: $\chi_{\rho/\Delta}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$; with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the form quoted above.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant gives $\chi_{a}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=U\,\sech U/[1+U\tanh U]$, which coincides with the permeable-base $\chi$ to $O(U)$: $\chi_{a}=U+O(U^{3})$, $\chi_{a}\sim2U e^{-U}$ for $U\gg1$. Current round colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 all recover the permeable-base result $\chi=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and note the $U\ll1$ limit $\chi\simeq U$. Sign conventions differ but magnitude is as above. ∎
reflection_text.7:
The stream-function/biharmonic formulation is now stable across the round.
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ from the rigid no-slip lid $u_x(0)=0$ and steady $u_z(0)=0$.
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, $\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Top normal stress: $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\Delta\rho g e$, i.e. $\Delta\rho g e=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ with $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-dk^{-1}z\sinh kz$
gives $P(z)=2\mu[-kc\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$ and $\Phi'''(z)-k^{2}\Phi'(z)=2k^{2}c\cosh kz-2k d\sinh kz$.

Base conditions used in the stated problem are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ with $u_z$ free at the base.  
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\Rightarrow P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\Rightarrow\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
These give
$(c+dh)\cosh kh =k c h\sinh kh$, 
$d=c\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$,
$2\mu c\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]/\big(h\cosh kh\big)=S_{0}$,
hence
$c= S_{0}h\cosh kh/\big\{2\mu\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]\big\}$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k c$ and
$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
\chi_{A}(kh)$,
$\displaystyle\chi_{A}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
       =\Big[\,U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\Big]^{-1}$,
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$, viscosity independent in steady state.

Long wave $U\ll1$:
$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$, $\chi_{A}=U+O(U^{3})$,
$e_{s}\simeq U S_{0}/\Delta\rho g =kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the quoted thin-plate dynamic topography $e_{s}\approx(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $W(h)=0\iff \Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant used by several colleagues gives the commonly quoted lubrication transfer
$\chi_{B}(U)=U/\big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\big]=1/\big[\sinh U+\cosh U/U\big]$,
$\chi_{B}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and $\chi_{B}\sim U\operatorname{sech}U$ for $U\gg1$.
$\chi_{A}$ and $\chi_{B}$ coincide to $O(U)$; the difference is the $O(1)$ $W(h)=0$ vs free vertical motion at the base. Both give the universal thin-plate limit $\chi\approx kh$ and the $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling. Sign conventions differ by an overall sign.

Unresolved/note: exact normalisation $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$. With the buoyant restoring stress the conventional form is $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi$ above, i.e. $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$. This is the steady viscous topographic response normally quoted.
reflection_text.5:
The current round confirms the stream-function analysis of round 1. With
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, the rigid impermeable lid is
$\Phi(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ in the steady state.  Up to rigid-body motion
$\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Cz\sinh kz$,
$ \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$ and

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$p=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx$.

The free lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e$,
i.e. $\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}A$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

At the base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ is $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_0$.
With $u=kh$,

$A\big( u\sinh u-\cosh u\big)=Ch\cosh u$,

$-2\mu kA\,(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)/(h\cosh u)=S_{0}$,
whence

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi(u)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$, 
$\displaystyle\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}$,
$u=kh$, independent of $\mu$.  

For $u\ll1$, $\cosh u=1+O(u^{2})$,
$\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3})$ and

$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

the usual long-wave viscous dynamic-topography scaling.  The
$kh/(\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh)$ family quoted by Colleagues 2,5,6 is the
$W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, impermeable-base variant
$\chi_{L}=u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u]$ which coincides with $\chi$ to $O(u)$.
Colleague 7’s $u/[\cosh u+u\sinh u+u^{2}/2]$ is the $O(kW)$ correction
to the basal shear condition.  Sign conventions differ by an overall
minus sign.  The essential physics is the $S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ scaling
with shape factor $\sim kh$, viscosity dropping out of the steady
balance, and the exact Stokes transfer function above is the one
required by $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e$. ∎

8.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e. $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the rigid impermeable lid is

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

so that up to an inessential constant

$\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-d k^{-1}z\sinh kz$

and

$P(z)=2\mu\big[-kc\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big]$.

On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=2\mu k\big(B+D\big)\cos kx
      =2\mu kc\cos kx$ .

With the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kc$,

and the normal stress free permeable base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$\big(c+d h\big)\cosh kh=kc\,h\sinh kh$,

i.e. $d=c\big[k\tanh kh-1/h\big]$.

The imposed basal shear

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}$

gives with $U=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh U$,

$S_{0}=2\mu c\,\dfrac{C_{h}^{2}+U^{2}}{hC_{h}}$,

hence

$c=\dfrac{S_{0}hC_{h}}{2\mu\big[U^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]}$.

Eliminating $c$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k c
      =S_{0}\;\dfrac{U C_{h}}{U^{2}+C_{h}^{2}},\qquad U=kh,$

i.e. in the conventional normalisation

$e_{s}=\chi(U)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle 
\chi_{\rho}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh$ ,

independent of $\mu$ in the steady state.  With the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
identification this is the exact Stokes transfer function for
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda
\ll1$,

$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$ and

$\chi(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
       =U+O(U^{3})$ ,

so that

$e_{s}\simeq U\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =kh\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$ ,

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling.  In the
$W(h)=0$ impermeable-base lubrication normalisation this is often
written as

$\chi_{L}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, which coincides with the exact
$\chi_{\rho}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$.  The sign is the sign of $S_{0}$; the magnitude is
the $U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ transfer function, $ \chi\simeq kh$
for $kh\ll1$. ∎

4.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi (x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx ,\qquad \nabla^{4}\psi =0,
$$

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
$$

the rigid impermeable lid

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0 ,
$$

gives up to an additive constant

$$
\Phi(z)=A\sinh kz+Bz\sinh kz-Akz\cosh kz ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ 

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx
      =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

so that with $\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$

$$
\Delta\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}A,\qquad 
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The dynamic conditions at $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx
$$

are

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0},
$$

i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.  With $U=kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh U$,
$s_{h}=\sinh U$ the normal stress condition gives

$$
A+Bh=A\,U\,\frac{s_{h}}{c_{h}},\qquad 
B=A\Big[\frac{U s_{h}}{c_{h}}-\frac1h\Big],
$$

and

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]
=2\mu k\Big[Bc_{h}+BU s_{h}-Ak^{2}h c_{h}\Big]=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $B$,

$$
2\mu kA\frac{c_{h}^{2}+U^{2}}{h c_{h}}=-S_{0},
$$

and with $A=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\,c_{h}}{c_{h}^{2}+U^{2}} .
$$

Hence on the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(U)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad U=kh,
$$

which is $\mu$–independent.  In particular

$$
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi(U)\sim2U e^{-2U},\qquad U\to\infty,
$$

so that on the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling, the sign being that
of $S_{0}$.  With the conventional impermeable base normalisation
$W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, the transfer function is usually written
in the equivalent lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U},
\qquad\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with the free-base Stokes function above to $O(U)$ and
is the $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ form most often quoted in
the literature.  Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification this is the steady Stokes transfer $e_{s}\propto
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with shape factor $\chi\simeq kh$.  The
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the buoyant restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎

3.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e.

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx
        =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

The rigid free lid is in the steady state

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0,
$$

so that with $C=-A$

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},\qquad C=-A,\;D=-B-2kA,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0) .
$$

Hence on the lid

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =\rho g e_{s}\cos kx ,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e_{s} .
$$

At the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=
2\mu A\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
$$

Eliminating $A$ with $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_{s}/\mu$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad U\equiv kh ,
$$

i.e. with the usual buoyant normalisation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(U)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
$$

which is $\mu$ independent.  In particular

$$
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi(U)\sim 2U e^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

so that to leading order

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh,
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography
scaling.  With the conventional $W(h)=0$ impermeable base
normalisation this is written as

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh U+\cosh U/U},
\qquad 
\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with the exact $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ transfer function
to $O(U)$ and gives the quoted $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
long wave limit.  Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification this is $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rho}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$.  The sign is the sign
convention for $S_{0}$; with the usual geophysical sign
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

6.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\;,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx\;,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx\;,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] .
$$

On the rigid free lid $u_{x}(0)=0$, $ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in the
steady state and

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that with the buoyant normalisation $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s}\;,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) .
$$

Up to rigid body motion

$$
\Phi(z)=A\,z\sinh kz+B\Big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(z)=2\mu k\Big[B\cosh kz-
kz\big(A\cosh kz+B\sinh kz\big)\Big]\cos kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}(z)=2\mu k\Big[A\cosh kz+kz
\big(A\sinh kz+B\cosh kz\big)\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the lid

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu kB\cos kx=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx,
\qquad 
B=\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k},
\tag{2}
$$

and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
B\cosh kh-kh\big(A\cosh kh+B\sinh kh\big)=0,
\qquad 
A=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
\tag{3}
$$

The imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ is

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[A\cosh kh+kh\big(A\sinh kh+B\cosh kh\big)\Big]
     =2\mu kB\,\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh},
$$

so that with (2)-(3)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. with $U=kh$ and the conventional buoyant normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi(U)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
       =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\tag{4}
$$

the viscosity drops out of the steady balance.  In the usual
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ notation $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rho}$ given by (4) and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is
trivial.

In particular

$$
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,
\qquad 
\chi(U)\sim2U e^{-2U},\qquad U\to\infty,
$$

so that on the geophysically relevant long-wave thin plate
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}), 
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh,
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling $e_{s}\propto
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the shape factor $kh$.  With the
conventional $W(h)=0$ impermeable–base normalisation this is usually
written in the equivalent lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U},
\qquad \chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})\;\;(U\ll1),
$$

which coincides with (4) to $O(U)$ and gives the quoted
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ long-wave limit.  The sign is
that of $S_{0}$; with the opposite sign convention
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

5.text:
With the harmonic ansatz
$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx,
$$
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is
$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
$$
and with the rigid free lid
$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$
up to rigid body motion
$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Cz\sinh kz  .
$$
With
$$
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$
P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$
the free lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$
so that on the steady state
$$
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}\;,
$$
i.e.
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A .
$$
The dynamic conditions at $z=h$ are
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0} .
$$
Writing $u=kh$ and using $\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0$ the normal stress
condition at the base is
$$
A\big[u\sinh u-\cosh u\big]=Ch\cosh u ,
$$
and the shear condition is
$$
-2\mu kA\,
\frac{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}{h\cosh u}=S_{0} .
$$
Eliminating $A,C$ with $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A$ gives the
steady Stokes transfer function
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$
i.e. with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi(u)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
$$
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad u=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\;,
$$
which is $\mu$-independent.  In particular
$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\qquad u\to0,
$$
so that on the geophysically relevant long-wave thin plate limit
$u=kh\ll1$, $\cosh u\simeq1$,
$$
\chi_{LW}(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq u\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$
the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling $e_{s}\propto
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the viscous shape factor $kh$.  With the
conventional impermeable base normalisation $W(h)=\Phi(h)=0$ this is
usually quoted in the lubrication form
$$
\chi_{L}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u},
\qquad \chi_{L}=u+O(u^{3})\;\;\hbox{for}\;\;u\ll1,
$$
which coincides with $\chi(u)$ to $O(u)$ and gives the textbook
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit.  Up to the
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation this is the
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous transfer function, viscosity
dropping out of the steady balance and sign being that of $S_{0}$.
∎

2.text:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ gives

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that on the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=\dot e$ and in the steady
state

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
\qquad 
P(0)=2\mu k\,(B+D) ,
$$

up to the sign convention.  Writing

$$
\Phi(z)=\Big(A+Bz\Big)e^{kz}+\Big(C+Dz\Big)e^{-kz},\qquad C=-A,
$$

$$
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,
$$

the base conditions which are imposed in the statement are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx ,
$$

i.e. $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ and 
$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}$ , with $u_{z}(h)$ free.
With $U=kh$ and the lid conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ this gives

$$
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{4\mu k^{2}},\qquad B+D=-2kA,
$$

$$
A\big(e^{U}+e^{-U}\big)+h\big(Be^{U}-De^{-U}\big)=0,
$$

$$
S_{0}=2\mu\Big[e^{U}\big(k^{2}A+kB(1+U)\big)
+e^{-U}\big(-k^{2}A-kD(1-U)\big)\Big],
$$

whence on elimination of $B,D$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}\;,
\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. with the normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
=\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh,
$$

which is $\mu$–independent.  With the usual buoyant restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is the exact Stokes
transfer for the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
conditions, $e_{s}\propto\pm S_{0}$ according to sign convention.

In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty .
$$

Hence on the geophysically relevant long wave thin-plate limit
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\chi_{LW}=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling.  The viscosity
drops out of the steady balance.  With the conventional $W(h)=0$
impermeable-base normalisation the usually quoted lubrication form is

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U},
$$

which satisfies $\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and coincides with
$\chi_{{\rm ex}}$ to $O(U)$.  Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow
\Delta\rho$ identification this is the $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ law, i.e. $\chi\approx kh=2\pi h/\lambda$ in the
thin-plate long-wave limit, the full Stokes form being
$\chi=U\cosh U\big/U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big$.  The sign is the sign of
$S_{0}$. ∎

1.text:
In the harmonic ansatz

$\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $\;u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$\nabla ^{4}\psi =0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$ and
with the rigid free lid

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in the steady state

$\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz\,e^{kz}+dz\,e^{-kz},\qquad d=-2ka-b$,
$U=kh$ .

Then

$\sigma_{zz}=\big[-P-2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$P(z)=-{\mu}/{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
so that on the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx$, $P(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$,
$b+d=-2ka$,

$\rho g e_{s}\cos kx=\sigma_{zz}(0)=4\mu k^{2}a\cos kx$, 
i.e.

$\rho g e_{s}=4\mu k^{2}a$.                           \tag{1}

The base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ are

$p(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, $\;\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$,
i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, which with $U=kh$ gives

$ak\big[\cosh U+Ue^{-U}\big]+Ub\cosh U=0$,
$ak\big[\cosh U-Ue^{-U}\big]+b\big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\big]=S_{0}/4\mu k,$

whence

$b=\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k}\,
\frac{\cosh U+Ue^{-U}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}},\qquad
a=-\frac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}}  $.

From (1)

$e_{s}= \frac{2\mu k}{\rho g} (b+d)=\frac{2\mu k}{\rho g}(-2ka)
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,$

so that the viscosity drops out of the steady balance.  On the
usual buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
this is

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(U)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
  =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,$

and with the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification

$e_{s}= \chi(U)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(U)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
        \dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},
\qquad U=kh,$

i.e. on the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;.$

In particular

$\chi_{\rho}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\;U\to0,\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(U)\sim2U e^{-U},\,U\to\infty,$

so that for the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate,
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$\chi_{\rho}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad
e_{s}\simeq U\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
      =kh\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling

$e_{s}\simeq\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$ .

With the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the often quoted
lubrication transfer
$\chi_{L}(U)=U\big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\big]^{-1}
          =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$, which coincides with
$\chi_{\rho}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
long wave limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Up to the
trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement this is the
steady Stokes transfer function for a harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$.  The sign is chosen so that $e_{s}>0$ for $S_{0}>0$.
This is the $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous topographic law,
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, normally quoted as
$\chi\approx kh=2\pi h/\lambda$ in the thin-plate long-wave limit. ∎

public_text.8:
With the harmonic ansatz

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e. $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$.

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the rigid impermeable lid is

$\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0$,

so that up to an inessential constant

$\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-d k^{-1}z\sinh kz$

and

$P(z)=2\mu\big[-kc\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big]$.

On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ and

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=2\mu k\big(B+D\big)\cos kx
      =2\mu kc\cos kx$ .

With the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g
e\cos kx$

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu kc$,

and the normal stress free permeable base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$\big(c+d h\big)\cosh kh=kc\,h\sinh kh$,

i.e. $d=c\big[k\tanh kh-1/h\big]$.

The imposed basal shear

$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}$

gives with $U=kh$, $C_{h}=\cosh U$,

$S_{0}=2\mu c\,\dfrac{C_{h}^{2}+U^{2}}{hC_{h}}$,

hence

$c=\dfrac{S_{0}hC_{h}}{2\mu\big[U^{2}+C_{h}^{2}\big]}$.

Eliminating $c$,

$\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k c
      =S_{0}\;\dfrac{U C_{h}}{U^{2}+C_{h}^{2}},\qquad U=kh,$

i.e. in the conventional normalisation

$e_{s}=\chi(U)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

$\displaystyle 
\chi_{\rho}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh$ ,

independent of $\mu$ in the steady state.  With the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
identification this is the exact Stokes transfer function for
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda
\ll1$,

$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$ and

$\chi(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
       =U+O(U^{3})$ ,

so that

$e_{s}\simeq U\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =kh\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$ ,

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling.  In the
$W(h)=0$ impermeable-base lubrication normalisation this is often
written as

$\chi_{L}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}$,

$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, which coincides with the exact
$\chi_{\rho}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$.  The sign is the sign of $S_{0}$; the magnitude is
the $U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ transfer function, $ \chi\simeq kh$
for $kh\ll1$. ∎
public_text.4:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi (x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,
$$

$$
p=P(z)\cos kx ,\qquad \nabla^{4}\psi =0,
$$

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
$$

the rigid impermeable lid

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0 ,
$$

gives up to an additive constant

$$
\Phi(z)=A\sinh kz+Bz\sinh kz-Akz\cosh kz ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ 

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx
      =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

so that with $\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$

$$
\Delta\rho g e=-2\mu k^{2}A,\qquad 
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e}{2\mu k^{2}} .
$$

The dynamic conditions at $z=h$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx
$$

are

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0},
$$

i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.  With $U=kh$, $c_{h}=\cosh U$,
$s_{h}=\sinh U$ the normal stress condition gives

$$
A+Bh=A\,U\,\frac{s_{h}}{c_{h}},\qquad 
B=A\Big[\frac{U s_{h}}{c_{h}}-\frac1h\Big],
$$

and

$$
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]
=2\mu k\Big[Bc_{h}+BU s_{h}-Ak^{2}h c_{h}\Big]=S_{0}.
$$

Eliminating $B$,

$$
2\mu kA\frac{c_{h}^{2}+U^{2}}{h c_{h}}=-S_{0},
$$

and with $A=-\Delta\rho g e_{s}/2\mu k^{2}$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\,c_{h}}{c_{h}^{2}+U^{2}} .
$$

Hence on the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
e_{s}= \chi(U)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad 
\chi(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad U=kh,
$$

which is $\mu$–independent.  In particular

$$
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi(U)\sim2U e^{-2U},\qquad U\to\infty,
$$

so that on the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling, the sign being that
of $S_{0}$.  With the conventional impermeable base normalisation
$W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, the transfer function is usually written
in the equivalent lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U},
\qquad\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with the free-base Stokes function above to $O(U)$ and
is the $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ form most often quoted in
the literature.  Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification this is the steady Stokes transfer $e_{s}\propto
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with shape factor $\chi\simeq kh$.  The
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the buoyant restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$. ∎
public_text.3:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$, i.e.

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx
        =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

The rigid free lid is in the steady state

$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0,
$$

so that with $C=-A$

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},\qquad C=-A,\;D=-B-2kA,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0) .
$$

Hence on the lid

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =\rho g e_{s}\cos kx ,\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e_{s} .
$$

At the base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=
2\mu A\frac{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
$$

Eliminating $A$ with $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e_{s}/\mu$,

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},\qquad U\equiv kh ,
$$

i.e. with the usual buoyant normalisation
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi(U)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
$$

which is $\mu$ independent.  In particular

$$
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi(U)\sim 2U e^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

so that to leading order

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh,
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography
scaling.  With the conventional $W(h)=0$ impermeable base
normalisation this is written as

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh U+\cosh U/U},
\qquad 
\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with the exact $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ transfer function
to $O(U)$ and gives the quoted $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
long wave limit.  Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification this is $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rho}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$.  The sign is the sign
convention for $S_{0}$; with the usual geophysical sign
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎
public_text.6:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx\;,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx\;,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx\;,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] .
$$

On the rigid free lid $u_{x}(0)=0$, $ \Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in the
steady state and

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
      =\rho g e\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that with the buoyant normalisation $\rho\to\Delta\rho$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s}\;,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h) .
$$

Up to rigid body motion

$$
\Phi(z)=A\,z\sinh kz+B\Big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(z)=2\mu k\Big[B\cosh kz-
kz\big(A\cosh kz+B\sinh kz\big)\Big]\cos kx,
$$

$$
\sigma_{xz}(z)=2\mu k\Big[A\cosh kz+kz
\big(A\sinh kz+B\cosh kz\big)\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the lid

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu kB\cos kx=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx,
\qquad 
B=\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k},
\tag{2}
$$

and $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives

$$
B\cosh kh-kh\big(A\cosh kh+B\sinh kh\big)=0,
\qquad 
A=B\,\frac{\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh}{kh\cosh kh}.
\tag{3}
$$

The imposed basal shear $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ is

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[A\cosh kh+kh\big(A\sinh kh+B\cosh kh\big)\Big]
     =2\mu kB\,\frac{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}{kh\cosh kh},
$$

so that with (2)-(3)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
$$

i.e. with $U=kh$ and the conventional buoyant normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi(U)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
       =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\tag{4}
$$

the viscosity drops out of the steady balance.  In the usual
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ notation $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with
$\chi_{\rho}$ given by (4) and the $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor is
trivial.

In particular

$$
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,
\qquad 
\chi(U)\sim2U e^{-2U},\qquad U\to\infty,
$$

so that on the geophysically relevant long-wave thin plate
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3}), 
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh,
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling $e_{s}\propto
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the shape factor $kh$.  With the
conventional $W(h)=0$ impermeable–base normalisation this is usually
written in the equivalent lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U},
\qquad \chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})\;\;(U\ll1),
$$

which coincides with (4) to $O(U)$ and gives the quoted
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ long-wave limit.  The sign is
that of $S_{0}$; with the opposite sign convention
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎
public_text.5:
With the harmonic ansatz
$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx,
$$
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is
$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
$$
and with the rigid free lid
$$
\Phi(0)=0,\qquad \Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$
up to rigid body motion
$$
\Phi(z)=A\Big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\Big]+Cz\sinh kz  .
$$
With
$$
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx ,
$$
$$
P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$
the free lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives
$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$
so that on the steady state
$$
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}\;,
$$
i.e.
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A .
$$
The dynamic conditions at $z=h$ are
$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0} .
$$
Writing $u=kh$ and using $\Phi'(0)=\Phi(0)=0$ the normal stress
condition at the base is
$$
A\big[u\sinh u-\cosh u\big]=Ch\cosh u ,
$$
and the shear condition is
$$
-2\mu kA\,
\frac{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}{h\cosh u}=S_{0} .
$$
Eliminating $A,C$ with $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A$ gives the
steady Stokes transfer function
$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$
i.e. with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi(u)\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
$$
\chi(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1},
\qquad u=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\;,
$$
which is $\mu$-independent.  In particular
$$
\chi(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\qquad u\to0,
$$
so that on the geophysically relevant long-wave thin plate limit
$u=kh\ll1$, $\cosh u\simeq1$,
$$
\chi_{LW}(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq u\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$
the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling $e_{s}\propto
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the viscous shape factor $kh$.  With the
conventional impermeable base normalisation $W(h)=\Phi(h)=0$ this is
usually quoted in the lubrication form
$$
\chi_{L}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u},
\qquad \chi_{L}=u+O(u^{3})\;\;\hbox{for}\;\;u\ll1,
$$
which coincides with $\chi(u)$ to $O(u)$ and gives the textbook
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ limit.  Up to the
$\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation this is the
$e_{s}= \chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous transfer function, viscosity
dropping out of the steady balance and sign being that of $S_{0}$.
∎
public_text.2:
With the harmonic ansatz

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ gives

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,
$$

so that on the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$, $w(0)=\dot e$ and in the steady
state

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
\qquad 
P(0)=2\mu k\,(B+D) ,
$$

up to the sign convention.  Writing

$$
\Phi(z)=\Big(A+Bz\Big)e^{kz}+\Big(C+Dz\Big)e^{-kz},\qquad C=-A,
$$

$$
P(z)=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx ,
$$

the base conditions which are imposed in the statement are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx ,
$$

i.e. $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ and 
$\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}$ , with $u_{z}(h)$ free.
With $U=kh$ and the lid conditions $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ this gives

$$
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{4\mu k^{2}},\qquad B+D=-2kA,
$$

$$
A\big(e^{U}+e^{-U}\big)+h\big(Be^{U}-De^{-U}\big)=0,
$$

$$
S_{0}=2\mu\Big[e^{U}\big(k^{2}A+kB(1+U)\big)
+e^{-U}\big(-k^{2}A-kD(1-U)\big)\Big],
$$

whence on elimination of $B,D$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}\;,
\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. with the normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
=\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh,
$$

which is $\mu$–independent.  With the usual buoyant restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ this is the exact Stokes
transfer for the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$
conditions, $e_{s}\propto\pm S_{0}$ according to sign convention.

In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty .
$$

Hence on the geophysically relevant long wave thin-plate limit
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\chi_{LW}=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling.  The viscosity
drops out of the steady balance.  With the conventional $W(h)=0$
impermeable-base normalisation the usually quoted lubrication form is

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\frac{1}{\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U},
$$

which satisfies $\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and coincides with
$\chi_{{\rm ex}}$ to $O(U)$.  Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow
\Delta\rho$ identification this is the $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$ law, i.e. $\chi\approx kh=2\pi h/\lambda$ in the
thin-plate long-wave limit, the full Stokes form being
$\chi=U\cosh U\big/U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big$.  The sign is the sign of
$S_{0}$. ∎
public_text.1:
In the harmonic ansatz

$\psi =\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $\;u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$\nabla ^{4}\psi =0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$ and
with the rigid free lid

$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in the steady state

$\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz\,e^{kz}+dz\,e^{-kz},\qquad d=-2ka-b$,
$U=kh$ .

Then

$\sigma_{zz}=\big[-P-2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx$,
$P(z)=-{\mu}/{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big]$,
so that on the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx$, $P(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$,
$b+d=-2ka$,

$\rho g e_{s}\cos kx=\sigma_{zz}(0)=4\mu k^{2}a\cos kx$, 
i.e.

$\rho g e_{s}=4\mu k^{2}a$.                           \tag{1}

The base conditions $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ are

$p(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, $\;\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$,
i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, which with $U=kh$ gives

$ak\big[\cosh U+Ue^{-U}\big]+Ub\cosh U=0$,
$ak\big[\cosh U-Ue^{-U}\big]+b\big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\big]=S_{0}/4\mu k,$

whence

$b=\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k}\,
\frac{\cosh U+Ue^{-U}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}},\qquad
a=-\frac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^{2}}\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}}  $.

From (1)

$e_{s}= \frac{2\mu k}{\rho g} (b+d)=\frac{2\mu k}{\rho g}(-2ka)
     =\frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
       \frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,$

so that the viscosity drops out of the steady balance.  On the
usual buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
this is

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}(U)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
  =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,$

and with the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification

$e_{s}= \chi(U)\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(U)=\dfrac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
        \dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},
\qquad U=kh,$

i.e. on the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ normalisation

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       \dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}\;.$

In particular

$\chi_{\rho}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\;U\to0,\qquad
\chi_{\rho}(U)\sim2U e^{-U},\,U\to\infty,$

so that for the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate,
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$\chi_{\rho}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad
e_{s}\simeq U\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\rho g}
      =kh\,\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}+O\big((kh)^{3}\big),$

the familiar viscous dynamic topography scaling

$e_{s}\simeq\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$ .

With the conventional $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the often quoted
lubrication transfer
$\chi_{L}(U)=U\big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\big]^{-1}
          =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$, which coincides with
$\chi_{\rho}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
long wave limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Up to the
trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement this is the
steady Stokes transfer function for a harmonic basal shear
$S_{0}\sin kx$.  The sign is chosen so that $e_{s}>0$ for $S_{0}>0$.
This is the $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous topographic law,
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, normally quoted as
$\chi\approx kh=2\pi h/\lambda$ in the thin-plate long-wave limit. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The linear Stokes problem is most conveniently written with a stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$, i.e. $\Phi^{iv}-2k^2\Phi''+k^4\Phi=0$. Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in the steady state. 

With the free lid normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, the biharmonic solution satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ can be written as $\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz e^{kz}+dz e^{-kz}$ with $d=-2ka-b$. Then $P(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$, $b+d=-2ka$ and $\rho g e_s=4\mu k^2 a$. 

Base conditions stated are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ or $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, and prescribed shear $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$. With $U=kh$ this gives 
$a k[\cosh U+U e^{-U}]+U b\cosh U=0$,
$a k[\cosh U-U e^{-U}]+b[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=S_0/4\mu k$,
whence 
$b=\frac{S_0}{4\mu k}\frac{\cosh U+U e^{-U}}{\cosh^2U+U^2}$,
$a=-\frac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^2}\frac{S_0}{\cosh^2U+U^2}$.

Hence $\rho g e_s =4\mu k^2 a$ gives the $\mu$–independent steady balance
$e_s=\frac{S_0}{\rho g}\frac{U\cosh U}{U^2+\cosh^2U}$,
$U=kh$, i.e. with the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$e_s=\chi(U)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi_\rho(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^2+\cosh^2U}
 =\big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\big]^{-1}$.
With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification $\chi(U)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\frac{U\cosh U}{U^2+\cosh^2U}$ and on the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ normalisation
$e_s=\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh}$.

Asymptotics: $\chi_\rho(U)=U+O(U^3)$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_\rho\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$. Long–wave thin plate $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$ gives $\chi\approx U$ and
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

All colleagues 1–8 in round 2 recover this exact transfer. The frequently quoted lubrication/impermeable base normalisation $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ gives the equivalent form
$\chi_L(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}=[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U]^{-1}$,
which satisfies $\chi_L=U+O(U^3)$ and coincides with $\chi_\rho$ to $O(U)$. The exact $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free–vertical–motion solution is the $U\cosh U/(U^2+\cosh^2U)$ form; the $U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]$ form is the $W(h)=0$ variant often quoted in the literature. Sign is a convention; magnitude is as above. Unresolved is only the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation and overall sign convention for $S_0$.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes harmonic problem is now settled in the group. With the stream function ansatz 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$. 
Rigid free lid $u_x(0)=0$ in the steady state is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$. 
$\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives $\rho g e =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. 
Base conditions used in the statement are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.
$P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$. No $u_z(h)=0$ is imposed; the base is permeable.

Up to constants 
$\Phi(z)=Az\sinh kz+B[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz]$.
Then $B=\rho g e/2\mu k$ from the lid, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khA\cosh kh$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives
$S_{0}=2\mu k[A\cosh kh+khA\sinh kh+khB\cosh kh]$.
Eliminating $A,B$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$ with, up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification,

$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady balance. Long wave $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U\simeq1$,

$\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar thin-plate scaling $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with shape factor $kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$.

If the density in the free-surface condition is kept as $\rho$, the strict conversion to $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$: $\chi_{\rho/\Delta}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$; with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the form quoted above.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant is
$\chi_{a}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=U\,\sech U/[1+U\tanh U]$, which coincides with the permeable-base $\chi$ to $O(U)$: $\chi_{a}=U+O(U^{3})$, $\chi_{a}\sim2U e^{-U}$ for $U\gg1$. This is the lubrication form $\chi_{L}=U/(\cosh U+U\sinh U)$ often quoted in the literature.

Round 2 public responses: Colleagues 1-8 all recover the permeable-base exact transfer $\chi_{ex}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$, with the long-wave limit $\chi\simeq U=kh$. Sign conventions differ but magnitude is identical. All note viscosity independence of the steady state and the $kh\ll1$ limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. No substantive disagreement remains; the only remaining nuance is the $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ normalisation and the permeable vs impermeable base distinction, with the statement’s conditions corresponding to the permeable base result above. ∎

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream-function reduction is settled across rounds 1–2. With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$. The rigid impermeable lid in the steady state is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, and the dynamic stresses are

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.

With the free lid $\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. Hence with the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$, and viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

The base conditions imposed in the statement are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$. With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Cz\sinh kz$, $\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$.

Putting $u=kh$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $A[u\sinh u-\cosh u]=Ch\cosh u$, and the shear condition gives $-2\mu kA(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)/(h\cosh u)=S_{0}$. Eliminating $A,C$ with $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$,

i.e. with the conventional normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
   =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}$, $u=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\mu$-independent.  In particular

$\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=u+O(u^{3})$, $u\to0$, $\chi_{\rm ex}(u)\sim2u e^{-2u}\to0$, $u\to\infty$,

so the geophysically relevant long-wave thin-plate limit $u\ll1$ is

$\chi_{LW}\simeq u=kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar viscous dynamic-topography scaling $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Round-2 colleagues 1-8 all recover this exact Stokes transfer. The commonly quoted lubrication/ impermeable-base $W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, variant is

$\chi_{L}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
          =\big[\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u\big]^{-1}$,

with $\chi_{L}=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$ and $\chi_{L}\sim2u e^{-u}$ for $u\gg1$. It coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(u)$ and is the $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ form most often quoted in the literature. Colleagues 2,5,6,7,8 explicitly note the $W(h)=0$ normalisation; the $u^{2}/2$ correction mentioned by Colleague 7 is the $O(kW)$ correction to the basal shear condition.

Sign conventions differ by an overall minus sign depending on traction orientation; the magnitude is as above. The replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ is the buoyant restoring stress used in the statement. Viscosity drops out of the steady balance, the shape factor is a function only of $kh$, and the long-wave limit is $\chi\simeq kh$. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion has converged on the same steady Stokes transfer. 
With the stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0$, $\Phi^{iv}-2k^2\Phi''+k^4\Phi=0$.  Rigid impermeable lid
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$.  Then
$\sigma_{zz}= -[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.
On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. $\rho g e_s= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.
Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$, with $w(h)$ free.

The solution satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ can be written
$\Phi=A\sinh kz+Bz\sinh kz-Akz\cosh kz$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.
Then $P(0)=-2\mu k^2A$, $\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2A$, $A=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$.
The base conditions give
$P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$,
which yields
$B=-A[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/h\cosh kh$ and
$-2\mu kA[\cosh^2 kh+(kh)^2]/h\cosh kh=S_0$.
Eliminating $A$,
$e_s = S_0/\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^2 kh+(kh)^2]$.
With the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big[(kh)^2+\cosh^2 kh\big]^{-1}
       =\big[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}$,

$\mu$-independent in the steady state. $U=kh$:
$\chi(U)=U\cosh U/(U^2+\cosh^2U)$, $\chi(U)=U+O(U^3)$ for $U\ll1$,
$\chi(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$.

Long-wave thin-plate limit $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$:
$\cosh U\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq U$, 
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g =2\pi h/\lambda\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
This is the viscosity-free dynamic-topography scaling quoted by all colleagues.

The frequently quoted impermeable-base / lubrication form 
$\chi_L(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+\cosh U/U]^{-1}$,
which follows from imposing $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$, coincides with the free-base
$\chi$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same long-wave limit $\chi_L=U+O(U^3)$.
Colleagues 1-8 all recover the same exact free-base transfer
$\chi_{\rm ex}=U\cosh U/(U^2+\cosh^2U)$ and the long-wave $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$.
Sign is a convention; magnitude is as above.  The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification is the only remaining notational difference.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Stokes stream-function solution with
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}= -[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Rigid free lid in steady state: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ and with $P(0)=-2\mu k(B+D)$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.  With
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
