$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$,

the two base conditions give

$A+Bh$ and $D$ related by $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.  Elimination
yields a $\mu$–independent steady balance

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\,k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\,}$,
$U=kh$,

i.e. with the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$e_{s}= \chi_{\rm ex}(U)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0$,

viscosity drops out of the steady state.  Long-wave thin-plate
$U\ll1$:

$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$, $\cosh U\simeq1$,

$e_{s}\simeq U S_{0}/\Delta\rho g =kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
 =(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous dynamic topography
scaling.  Sign is conventional; $e_{s}>0$ for $S_{0}>0$ with the chosen
orientation, $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is the usual buoyant identification.

The lubrication / impermeable base family

$\chi_{L}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
 =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}$,

i.e. $e_{s}= \chi_{L}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, follows from the extra
kinematic condition $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$.  It coincides
with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same long-wave limit
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$.  The statement as given imposes only
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not $W(h)=0$, so the exact Stokes transfer with the
stated boundary conditions is the $U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ form
above, reducing to $\chi\simeq kh$ for $kh\ll1$.  This is the consensus
of the round-2 derivations, up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
and sign conventions.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation is now essentially converged on the rigid-impermeable lid stream-function biharmonic solution with the steady kinematic lid
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, $u_z(0)=\dot e=0$, $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, 
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.

With $\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-d k^{-1}z\sinh kz$, $U=kh$,
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$, so in the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k c$. 
Base $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ give
$(c+d h)\cosh U=k c h\sinh U$, $d=c[k\sinh U/\cosh U-1/h]$ and
$2\mu[c h k^{2}\cosh U-d\cosh U-d h k\sinh U]=S_0$, i.e.
$c=S_0 h\cosh U/[2\mu\,(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)]$.

Hence in the steady state the viscosity drops out,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$,
$e_s=\chi(U)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
=\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1},\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}$,

which with the $\rho$ normalisation is $e_s=\chi_\rho S_0/\rho g$,
$\chi_\rho(U)=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$; $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ is trivial.

Long wave $U\ll1$: $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$, $\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, 
$e_s\simeq U S_0/\Delta\rho g =kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g
=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar viscous dynamic-topography scaling with $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$, $\mu$ independent.

The $W(h)=0$ impermeable-base/lubrication family
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U]^{-1}$,
and the $kW$ corrected form $\chi_7(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U+U^{2}/2]$,
are repeatedly quoted. They coincide with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and share the same $U\ll1$ limit $\chi\simeq U$; the difference is the $W(h)=0$ vs $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ / $kW$ basal-shear treatment. Sign is conventional, $e_s>0$ for $S_0>0$ up to sign convention. The earlier round-0 dispute between $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and $W'(0)=0$ only is resolved in favour of the rigid lid $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ steady solution above, which is now the common exact transfer function, with the thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$ the quoted geophysical result.

7.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The biharmonic stream-function formulation is now consistent across rounds.

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$.
Rigid no-slip lid at $z=0$ in steady state: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$.
$\sigma_{zz}= -[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.
Top: $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g e = \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$.

General solution satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$:
$\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-d k^{-1}z\sinh kz$,
$P(z)=2\mu[-kc\cosh kz+d\sinh kz]$, 
$\Phi'''(z)-k^{2}\Phi'(z)=2k^{2}c\cosh kz-2k d\sinh kz$.

Base conditions used in the statement: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$u_z$ free.  
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff (c+d h)\cosh kh=kc h\sinh kh$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.

This gives $d=c\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$ and
$2\mu c\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]/\big(h\cosh kh\big)=S_{0}$, i.e.

$c=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\big\{2\mu\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]\big\}$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k c$ and

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,\chi_{A}(U)$,
$\displaystyle\chi_{A}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\,U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\Big]^{-1}$, $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

viscosity independent in steady state. $ \chi_{A}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$,
$\chi_{A}\sim2U e^{-2U}$ for $U\gg1$. Thin-plate long wave:
$e_{s}\simeq U S_{0}/\Delta\rho g =kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. 
$e_{s}\simeq(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the quoted $ \chi_{LW}\simeq kh$.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant, used by several colleagues,
gives the lubrication transfer

$\chi_{B}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\dfrac{1}{\sinh U+\cosh U/U}$,
$\chi_{B}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and $\chi_{B}\sim U\operatorname{sech}U$ for $U\gg1$.
$\chi_{A}$ and $\chi_{B}$ coincide to $O(U)$; the difference is free vertical motion at the base vs $u_z(h)=0$.
All colleagues agree on viscosity dropping out, $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, and on the universal thin-plate limit $\chi\approx kh$.

Sign convention is $e_{s}>0$ for $S_{0}>0$ with the orientation used above; geophysical convention often flips sign.
Normalisation $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ in the statement $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$
is conventionally replaced by the buoyant restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$; the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$ is trivial.

Unresolved note remains the exact normalisation in the final quoted form, but the functional dependence $\chi(U)=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ with long-wave $\chi\approx kh$ is the stable consensus for the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free-base problem.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation has now converged on the Stokes stream-function
solution with

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$, 
$p=P(z)\cos kx$, $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$,

rigid impermeable lid $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$.
Then

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\Phi'''-3\mu k\Phi'$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

and on the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$,
so $ \Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$.

At the base the stated conditions are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$,
$\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$, $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$,
with $u_{z}(h)$ free.  With $\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$C=-A$, $B+D=-2kA$, $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, elimination of $A,B,D$ gives

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh$,

i.e. on the buoyant normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0$,
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

which is $\mu$-independent in the steady state.  In particular

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, 
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$.

Hence for the geophysically relevant long-wave thin-plate limit
$U=kh\ll1$

$\chi_{LW}\simeq U=kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}+O\big((kh)^{3}\big)$,

the familiar viscosity-free dynamic-topography scaling.  The sign is
the sign convention for $S_{0}$; with the conventional geophysical sign
$e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.

The lubrication / impermeable-base form

$\chi_{L}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}$,

is obtained if the extra kinematic condition $W(h)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$, is imposed at the base.  It satisfies
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$
to $O(U)$; it is the $kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ form most often
quoted in the literature.  The problem as stated imposes only
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not $W(h)=0$, so the exact Stokes transfer for the
stated conditions is $\chi_{\rm ex}$ above, which reduces to the
quoted $\chi\simeq kh$ thin-plate limit.  With the $\rho\to\Delta\rho$
identification the usual textbook expression is $e_{s}=
\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with $\chi_{\rho}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$
and $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ for $kh\ll1$.

reflection_text.1:
The linear Stokes problem is most conveniently written with a stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $\nabla^4\psi=0$, i.e. $\Phi^{iv}-2k^2\Phi''+k^4\Phi=0$. Rigid lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in the steady state. 

With the free lid normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$, $\sigma_{zz}=-[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, the biharmonic solution satisfying $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ can be written as $\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz e^{kz}+dz e^{-kz}$ with $d=-2ka-b$. Then $P(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$, $b+d=-2ka$ and $\rho g e_s=4\mu k^2 a$. 

Base conditions stated are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e. $P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$ or $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$, and prescribed shear $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$. With $U=kh$ this gives 
$a k[\cosh U+U e^{-U}]+U b\cosh U=0$,
$a k[\cosh U-U e^{-U}]+b[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=S_0/4\mu k$,
whence 
$b=\frac{S_0}{4\mu k}\frac{\cosh U+U e^{-U}}{\cosh^2U+U^2}$,
$a=-\frac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^2}\frac{S_0}{\cosh^2U+U^2}$.

Hence $\rho g e_s =4\mu k^2 a$ gives the $\mu$–independent steady balance
$e_s=\frac{S_0}{\rho g}\frac{U\cosh U}{U^2+\cosh^2U}$,
$U=kh$, i.e. with the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$e_s=\chi(U)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with
$\chi_\rho(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^2+\cosh^2U}
 =\big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\big]^{-1}$.
With the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification $\chi(U)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\frac{U\cosh U}{U^2+\cosh^2U}$ and on the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ normalisation
$e_s=\frac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^2+\cosh^2kh}$.

Asymptotics: $\chi_\rho(U)=U+O(U^3)$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_\rho\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$. Long–wave thin plate $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$ gives $\chi\approx U$ and
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

All colleagues 1–8 in round 2 recover this exact transfer. The frequently quoted lubrication/impermeable base normalisation $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ gives the equivalent form
$\chi_L(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}=[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U]^{-1}$,
which satisfies $\chi_L=U+O(U^3)$ and coincides with $\chi_\rho$ to $O(U)$. The exact $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free–vertical–motion solution is the $U\cosh U/(U^2+\cosh^2U)$ form; the $U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]$ form is the $W(h)=0$ variant often quoted in the literature. Sign is a convention; magnitude is as above. Unresolved is only the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation and overall sign convention for $S_0$.
reflection_text.6:
The Stokes harmonic problem is now settled in the group. With the stream function ansatz 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$. 
Rigid free lid $u_x(0)=0$ in the steady state is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$. 
$\sigma_{zz}=[-P-2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$.

$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ gives $\rho g e =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. 
Base conditions used in the statement are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, i.e.
$P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$. No $u_z(h)=0$ is imposed; the base is permeable.

Up to constants 
$\Phi(z)=Az\sinh kz+B[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz]$.
Then $B=\rho g e/2\mu k$ from the lid, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khA\cosh kh$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ gives
$S_{0}=2\mu k[A\cosh kh+khA\sinh kh+khB\cosh kh]$.
Eliminating $A,B$,

$\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{\cosh^{2}kh+(kh)^{2}}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_{s}= \chi(kh)\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$ with, up to the conventional $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification,

$\displaystyle\chi(kh)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}
      =\Big[\frac{kh}{\cosh kh}+\frac{\cosh kh}{kh}\Big]^{-1}$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady balance. Long wave $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U\simeq1$,

$\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar thin-plate scaling $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with shape factor $kh$, 
$e_{s}\simeq\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$.

If the density in the free-surface condition is kept as $\rho$, the strict conversion to $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ carries the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$: $\chi_{\rho/\Delta}= (\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$; with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the form quoted above.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant is
$\chi_{a}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=U\,\sech U/[1+U\tanh U]$, which coincides with the permeable-base $\chi$ to $O(U)$: $\chi_{a}=U+O(U^{3})$, $\chi_{a}\sim2U e^{-U}$ for $U\gg1$. This is the lubrication form $\chi_{L}=U/(\cosh U+U\sinh U)$ often quoted in the literature.

Sign conventions differ but magnitude is identical. All note viscosity independence of the steady state and the $kh\ll1$ limit $e_{s}\approx kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. No substantive disagreement remains; the only remaining nuance is the $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ normalisation and the permeable vs impermeable base distinction, with the statement’s conditions corresponding to the permeable base result above. ∎

The base conditions imposed in the statement are $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$. With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Cz\sinh kz$, $\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$.

Putting $u=kh$, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $A[u\sinh u-\cosh u]=Ch\cosh u$, and the shear condition gives $-2\mu kA(u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u)/(h\cosh u)=S_{0}$. Eliminating $A,C$ with $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A$,

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$,

i.e. with the conventional normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
   =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}$, $u=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\mu$-independent.  In particular

$\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=u+O(u^{3})$, $u\to0$, $\chi_{\rm ex}(u)\sim2u e^{-2u}\to0$, $u\to\infty$,

so the geophysically relevant long-wave thin-plate limit $u\ll1$ is

$\chi_{LW}\simeq u=kh$, $e_{s}\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar viscous dynamic-topography scaling $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Round-2 colleagues 1-8 all recover this exact Stokes transfer. The commonly quoted lubrication/ impermeable-base $W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$, variant is

$\chi_{L}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
          =\big[\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u\big]^{-1}$,

with $\chi_{L}=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\ll1$ and $\chi_{L}\sim2u e^{-u}$ for $u\gg1$. It coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(u)$ and is the $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ form most often quoted in the literature. Colleagues 2,5,6,7,8 explicitly note the $W(h)=0$ normalisation; the $u^{2}/2$ correction mentioned by Colleague 7 is the $O(kW)$ correction to the basal shear condition.

Sign conventions differ by an overall minus sign depending on traction orientation; the magnitude is as above. The replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e$ is the buoyant restoring stress used in the statement. Viscosity drops out of the steady balance, the shape factor is a function only of $kh$, and the long-wave limit is $\chi\simeq kh$. ∎
reflection_text.4:
The discussion has converged on the same steady Stokes transfer. 
With the stream function $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0$, $\Phi^{iv}-2k^2\Phi''+k^4\Phi=0$.  Rigid impermeable lid

$\sigma_{zz}= -[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$,

$\Phi=A\sinh kz+Bz\sinh kz-Akz\cosh kz$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$.
Then $P(0)=-2\mu k^2A$, $\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2A$, $A=-\rho g e_s/2\mu k^2$.
The base conditions give
$P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$,
which yields
$B=-A[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]/h\cosh kh$ and
$-2\mu kA[\cosh^2 kh+(kh)^2]/h\cosh kh=S_0$.
Eliminating $A$,
$e_s = S_0/\rho g\;kh\cosh kh/[\cosh^2 kh+(kh)^2]$.
With the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$,

$e_s=\chi(kh)S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi(kh)=kh\cosh kh\big[(kh)^2+\cosh^2 kh\big]^{-1}
       =\big[kh/\cosh kh+\cosh kh/kh\big]^{-1}$,

$\chi(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$.

$\cosh U\simeq1$, $\chi\simeq U$, 
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g =2\pi h/\lambda\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
This is the viscosity-free dynamic-topography scaling quoted by all colleagues.

The frequently quoted impermeable-base / lubrication form 
$\chi_L(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+\cosh U/U]^{-1}$,
which follows from imposing $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$, coincides with the free-base
$\chi$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same long-wave limit $\chi_L=U+O(U^3)$.

$\chi_{\rm ex}=U\cosh U/(U^2+\cosh^2U)$ and the long-wave $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$.

identification is the only remaining notational difference.

reflection_text.7:
The biharmonic stream-function formulation is now consistent across rounds.

$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$.
Rigid no-slip lid at $z=0$ in steady state: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$.
$\sigma_{zz}= -[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$,

Top: $\Phi'(0)=0$ gives $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.

$\Phi'''(z)-k^{2}\Phi'(z)=2k^{2}c\cosh kz-2k d\sinh kz$.

$2\mu c\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]/\big(h\cosh kh\big)=S_{0}$, i.e.

$c=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\big\{2\mu\big[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh\big]\big\}$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu k c$ and

$e_{s}= \dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,\chi_{A}(U)$,
$\displaystyle\chi_{A}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\,U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\Big]^{-1}$, $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

viscosity independent in steady state. $ \chi_{A}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$,

5.text:
With the harmonic stream function

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\;p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ is

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx
        =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

In the steady state the rigid lid is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ and on the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
          =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress the lid normal traction is
$\Delta\rho g e$.  On the rigid impermeable lid

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Cz\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},
$$

so that from (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A . \tag{2}
$$

The dynamic base conditions are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

i.e.

$$
A\big[u\sinh u-\cosh u\big]=Ch\cosh u ,\qquad 
-2\mu kA\,\frac{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}{h\cosh u}=S_{0} ,
$$

with $u=kh$.  Eliminating $A,C$ with (2)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

so that on the normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
       \qquad u=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

which is $\mu$ independent in the steady state and changes sign with
$S_{0}$.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\qquad u\to0, \qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)\sim2u\,e^{-2u}\to0,\qquad u\to\infty .
$$

Hence for the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate
$u=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\cosh u=1+O(u^{2}),\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=u+O(u^{3}),
$$

i.e. to leading order

$$
e_{s}\simeq u\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law
$e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional
impermeable base $W(h)=\Phi(h)=0$ normalisation this is usually quoted
in lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
          =\Big[\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u\Big]^{-1}
          =u+O(u^{3}),\qquad u\ll1,
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(u)$ and gives the same thin
plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Up to sign convention the sign is that of $S_{0}$, $e_{s}\simeq
-\,kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the usual geophysical sign convention.
The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the buoyant restoring
stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ used in the statement.
∎

$$

        =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=2\mu kc
      =S_{0}\,\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

i.e. in the conventional form

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{A}(U)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{A}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
          =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
 $$

which is $\mu$ independent.  In particular

$$
\chi_{A}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{A}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}, \qquad U\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$,

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi_{A}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

so that to leading order

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography scaling.
With the usual $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation this is quoted
in lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1},
\qquad \chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{A}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin plate
limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
identification the steady Stokes transfer is $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with the shape factor $kh$.  The sign is the sign of $S_{0}$; with the
usual geophysical sign convention $e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
This is $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ and in the strict
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free-base formulation
$\chi=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$. ∎

2.text:
With the harmonic stream function

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$

$$
 \sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx
          =\mu k^{-1}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
 \sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the rigid free lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ 

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx 
      =\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s} .
$$

Writing

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},\qquad C=-A,
$$

the lid conditions give $C=-A$, $B+D=-2kA$ and

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A .
$$

Hence

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A .
\tag{1}
$$

At the permeable base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad  
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}.
$$

With $U=kh$ and $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\; \Longrightarrow\; 
A\big(e^{U}+e^{-U}\big)+h\big(Be^{U}-De^{-U}\big)=0,
$$

and

$$
S_{0}=2\mu kA\,\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{U\cosh U}
      \;\;{\rm in\;terms\;of\; }A .
$$

Eliminating $A,B,D$ from (1) gives the $\mu$–free steady transfer

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. with $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0 ,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the viscosity drops out of the steady balance.  In particular

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,
\qquad 
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty .
$$

On the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$,
$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity–independent viscous dynamic topography law.
With the conventional impermeable base normalisation $W(h)=0$,
$\Phi(h)=0$, this is usually written in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1},
\qquad \chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{{\rm ex}}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  Up to the sign convention
$e_{s}\propto\pm S_{0}$ this is the quoted $e_{s}\approx kh\,
S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ dynamic topography scaling, viz. $\chi_{LW}\simeq
kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.  The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement
is the usual buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$.
The sign is reversed with the conventional geophysical sign
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

4.text:
With the harmonic stream function
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$ the Stokes equations give
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$,

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'] ,\qquad
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx
      =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

The rigid free lid is in the steady state
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ so that

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyant normalisation 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ on the lid and
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx$ at the base,

$$
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .
$$

Up to rigid motion the lid conditions give
$\Phi(z)=A\sinh kz+Bz\sinh kz-Akz\cosh kz$.  Then
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$, $P(0)=-2\mu k^{2}A$ and

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A .
$$

The base normal stress $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
and with $U=kh$

$$
B=A\Big[\frac{U\sinh U}{\cosh U}-\frac1h\Big],\qquad
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
 =2\mu kA\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{h\cosh U}=S_{0}.
$$

Hence

$$
A=-\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k^{2}},\qquad
2\mu kA\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{h\cosh U}= -S_{0},
$$

and the viscosity drops out of the steady balance,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

and $e_{s}\propto\pm S_{0}$ according to sign convention.  In
particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty,
$$

so that for the geophysically relevant long-wave thin plate
$U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography
scaling.  With the $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation this is
usually quoted in the lubrication form
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/\big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\big]=\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$, which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$
and gives the same thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.
Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement this is
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with the magnitude
$|\chi|\simeq kh$ and the exact free-base Stokes transfer
$|\chi|=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$.  With the usual geophysical sign
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

1.text:
With the harmonic stream function

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx
        =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the rigid free lid $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
$$

so that with the buoyant restoring stress

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx
$$

$$
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s},
\tag{1}
$$

and in the steady state $\dot e=0$.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz e^{kz}+dz e^{-kz},\qquad d=-2ka-b,
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(z)=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(z)=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

The permeable base conditions

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0}
$$

with $U=kh$ give on $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
ak\big[\cosh U+Ue^{-U}\big]+Ub\cosh U=0,
$$
$$
ak\big[\cosh U-Ue^{-U}\big]+b\big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\big]=\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k},
$$

i.e.

$$
b=\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k}\frac{\cosh U+Ue^{-U}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}},\qquad
a=-\frac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^{2}}\frac{S_{0}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}} .
$$

Now $P(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$,$b+d=-2ka$ and from (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=4\mu k^{2}a .
$$

Hence the viscosity drops out of the steady balance,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh ,
$$

i.e. with the conventional normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
   =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

and on the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ normalisation used in the statement

$$
e_{s}= \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g}\,
      \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh},
\qquad 
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}\,
       \frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}.
$$

In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\;U\to0,\qquad
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0,\;U\to\infty,
$$

so that for the geophysically relevant long wave thin–plate
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad \chi_{LW}\simeq kh,
$$

the familiar $\mu$–independent viscous dynamic topography scaling.
With the often used impermeable base normalisation $w(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$,
the transfer function is written in the equivalent lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1},
\qquad\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin
plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$, $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, up to
the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ sign convention.  The sign
is that of $S_{0}$; with the usual geophysical sign $e_{s}\simeq
-kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

8.text:
In the harmonic normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 , \qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx
      =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

The steady rigid lid is

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad \dot e=0 ,
$$

so that up to rigid motion

$$
\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-
d k^{-1}z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
P(z)=2\mu\big[-kc\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big] .
$$

On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =2\mu k c\cos kx ,
$$

so that with the buoyant restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k c\tag{1}
$$

in the steady state.  The dynamic base conditions

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx,
$$

are

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
 $$

i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.  With $U=kh$

$$
\big(c+d h\big)\cosh U=kc\,h\sinh U,
\qquad 
d=c\Big[\,k\tanh U-\frac1h\Big],
$$

and

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[Bc_{h}+BU s_{h}-Ak^{2}h c_{h}\Big]
    =2\mu c\,\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{h\cosh U},
$$

i.e.

$$
c=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh U}{2\mu\Big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\Big]}\; .
$$

Putting this in (1) the viscosity drops out of the steady balance,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},
\qquad U\equiv kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

so that on the conventional normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh,
$$

and with the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ notation $e_{s}=\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$
with the same $\chi_{\rho}$.  In particular

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U},\;U\to\infty ,
$$

so that for the geophysically relevant thin–plate long wave limit
$U=kh\ll1$

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law.
With the conventional $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation this is
written in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}
          =U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\ll1,
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{{\rm ex}}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
thin plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  Up to the sign convention
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=-S_{0}$ this is $e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the
usual $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous topographic transfer
with shape factor $kh$.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is trivial.
∎

and

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[A\cosh U+U A\sinh U+UB\cosh U\Big] .
\tag{3}
$$

Eliminating $A,B$ from (1)-(3) the viscosity drops out of the steady
balance and

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
     =\Bigg[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Bigg]^{-1}>0 ,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda} ,
$$

so that with the plate density $\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}\,
       \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g} .
$$

On the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is
the $\mu$-independent Stokes transfer

$$
e_{s}= \chi(U)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(U)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})\quad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\quad U\to\infty,
$$

so that for the thin plate long wave limit $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,
$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

i.e. up to sign $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the
conventional $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation this is usually
written in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1},
\qquad \chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{{\rm ex}}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the quoted
thin-plate viscous dynamic topography law $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The sign is that of $S_{0}$; with the
opposite geophysical sign convention $e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
This is the familiar $\chi\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$ viscous
topographic scaling, the viscosity dropping out of the steady
balance.  If the $\rho$ appearing in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ is
kept distinct from the buoyant $\Delta\rho$, the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$
is carried over, $\chi_{\rho/\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/
\big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big]\to(\rho/\Delta\rho)U$ for $U\ll1$. ∎

public_text.5:
With the harmonic stream function

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\;p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ is

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx
        =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

In the steady state the rigid lid is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$ and on the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
          =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress the lid normal traction is
$\Delta\rho g e$.  On the rigid impermeable lid

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Cz\sinh kz ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3},
$$

so that from (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A . \tag{2}
$$

The dynamic base conditions are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

i.e.

$$
A\big[u\sinh u-\cosh u\big]=Ch\cosh u ,\qquad 
-2\mu kA\,\frac{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}{h\cosh u}=S_{0} ,
$$

with $u=kh$.  Eliminating $A,C$ with (2)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

so that on the normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
       =\Big[\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
       \qquad u=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

which is $\mu$ independent in the steady state and changes sign with
$S_{0}$.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\qquad u\to0, \qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)\sim2u\,e^{-2u}\to0,\qquad u\to\infty .
$$

Hence for the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate
$u=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,

$$
\cosh u=1+O(u^{2}),\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=u+O(u^{3}),
$$

i.e. to leading order

$$
e_{s}\simeq u\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law
$e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the conventional
impermeable base $W(h)=\Phi(h)=0$ normalisation this is usually quoted
in lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
          =\Big[\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u\Big]^{-1}
          =u+O(u^{3}),\qquad u\ll1,
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(u)$ and gives the same thin
plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$ and $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Up to sign convention the sign is that of $S_{0}$, $e_{s}\simeq
-\,kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the usual geophysical sign convention.
The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is the buoyant restoring
stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ used in the statement.
∎

\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
       =2\mu k c\cos kx ,
$$

so that with the buoyant restoring stress
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k c\tag{1}
$$

in the steady state.  The dynamic base conditions

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\qquad \sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx,
$$

are

$$
P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0,\qquad 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
 $$

i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$.  With $U=kh$

$$
\big(c+d h\big)\cosh U=kc\,h\sinh U,
\qquad 
d=c\Big[\,k\tanh U-\frac1h\Big],
$$

and

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[Bc_{h}+BU s_{h}-Ak^{2}h c_{h}\Big]
    =2\mu c\,\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{h\cosh U},
$$

i.e.

$$
c=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh U}{2\mu\Big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\Big]}\; .
$$

Putting this in (1) the viscosity drops out of the steady balance,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},
\qquad U\equiv kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

so that on the conventional normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh,
$$

and with the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ notation $e_{s}=\chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$
with the same $\chi_{\rho}$.  In particular

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U},\;U\to\infty ,
$$

so that for the geophysically relevant thin–plate long wave limit
$U=kh\ll1$

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

i.e.

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law.
With the conventional $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation this is
written in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}
          =U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\ll1,
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{{\rm ex}}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
thin plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  Up to the sign convention
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=-S_{0}$ this is $e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the
usual $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ viscous topographic transfer
with shape factor $kh$.  The $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ replacement is trivial.
∎
public_text.3:
With the harmonic stream function

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx , \qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$$
\nabla^{4}\psi=0\;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,
$$

$$
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}=-\Big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\Big]\cos kx
        =\mu k^{-1}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,
$$
$$
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx  .
$$

On the rigid free lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ in the steady state

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,
$$

and with the buoyant restoring stress

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
\qquad \Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s} .
$$

Up to rigid motion

$$
\Phi(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)e^{kz}+\big(C+Dz\big)e^{-kz},\qquad
C=-A,
$$

and the lid conditions give $D=-B-2kA$.  The conditions imposed at the
base are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\Big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\Big]=S_{0},
$$

with $u_{z}(h)$ free.  Putting $U=kh$ the normal stress free base
condition is $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=
\frac{4\mu k^{2}A}{\,}\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=2\mu kA\,
\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{U\cosh U}=S_{0} .
$$

Eliminating $A$ with $\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_{s}/\mu$,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. on the conventional buoyant normalisation

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm ex}(U)\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}, \qquad
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
   =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0 ,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

which is $\mu$ independent in the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,
\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$,
$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$ and

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the usual viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography scaling.
With the sign convention $\sigma_{xz}(h)=-S_{0}$ this is
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Up to the conventional
impermeable base normalisation $W(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$, the transfer
function is often written in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}
          =U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\ll1,
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
thin-plate long-wave limit $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.
On the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ normalisation the familiar form is
$e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$, $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
with the shape factor $kh$.  This is the steady Stokes transfer
for the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0,\;\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ conditions,
the viscosity dropping out of the steady balance. ∎
public_text.6:
With the harmonic stream function

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi (z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx ,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi =0$ is $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$ and on the
rigid free lid $u_{x}(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)\cos kx=
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_{s},\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\!\left[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\right]\cos kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\!\left[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\right]\sin kx .
$$

Up to rigid motion

$$
\Phi(z)=Az\sinh kz+B\Big[\,z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\Big],
$$

so that on the lid

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=2\mu k B\cos kx=\Delta\rho g e_{s}\cos kx ,
\qquad B=\frac{\Delta\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k},
\tag{1}
$$

and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx .
$$

Putting $U=kh$ the normal stress free base gives

$$
B\big[\cosh U-U\sinh U\big]=U A\cosh U ,
\tag{2}
$$

and

$$
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[A\cosh U+U A\sinh U+UB\cosh U\Big] .
\tag{3}
$$

Eliminating $A,B$ from (1)-(3) the viscosity drops out of the steady
balance and

$$
\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. with the conventional notation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{{\rm ex}}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
     =\Bigg[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Bigg]^{-1}>0 ,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda} ,
$$

so that with the plate density $\rho$ used in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g
e\cos kx$

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}\,
       \frac{S_{0}}{\rho g} .
$$

On the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is
the $\mu$-independent Stokes transfer

$$
e_{s}= \chi(U)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi(U)=\frac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh} .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi(U)=U+O(U^{3})\quad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\quad U\to\infty,
$$

so that for the thin plate long wave limit $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$,
$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
       =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

i.e. up to sign $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the
conventional $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation this is usually
written in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1},
\qquad \chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{{\rm ex}}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the quoted
thin-plate viscous dynamic topography law $e_{s}\approx
kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  The sign is that of $S_{0}$; with the
opposite geophysical sign convention $e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
This is the familiar $\chi\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$ viscous
topographic scaling, the viscosity dropping out of the steady
balance.  If the $\rho$ appearing in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ is
kept distinct from the buoyant $\Delta\rho$, the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$
is carried over, $\chi_{\rho/\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/
\big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big]\to(\rho/\Delta\rho)U$ for $U\ll1$. ∎

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation has converged on the steady Stokes transfer for a viscous sheet with a rigid impermeable lid u_x(0)=0 and a traction-free normal base σ_zz(h)=0, imposed basal shear σ_xz(h)=S0 sin kx and buoyant lid normal stress σ_zz(0)=Δρ g e cos kx. With stream function ψ=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ' sin kx, u_z=-kΦ cos kx, p=P(z) cos kx,
∇⁴ψ=0 → Φⁱᵛ-2k²Φ''+k⁴Φ=0, P=-μ k⁻¹[Φ'''-k²Φ'], σ_zz=μ k⁻¹[Φ'''-3k²Φ'] cos kx, σ_xz=μ[Φ''+k²Φ] sin kx.
Lid: Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 → σ_zz(0)=-P(0)=μ k⁻¹Φ'''(0)=Δρ g e_s.
Base: σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ'''(h)=3k²Φ'(h), σ_xz(h)=S0 ⇔ μ[Φ''(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S0.
With Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 the solution can be written Φ=A sinh kz+ B z sinh kz -A k z cosh kz etc. Elimination gives μ independent steady balance

Δρ g e_s = S0 U cosh U /[U²+cosh² U],  U=kh=2π h/λ,

i.e. on the conventional normalisation e_s=χ(U)S0/Δρ g

χ_ex(U)=U cosh U/[U²+cosh² U]=[U/ cosh U+cosh U/U]⁻¹>0,

so that the viscosity drops out of the steady state.  Asymptotic behaviour
χ_ex=U+O(U³) for U≪1, χ_ex∼2U e^{-2U}→0 for U≫1.  Hence the geophysically relevant thin-plate long-wave limit

χ_LW≃U=kh=2π h/λ,   e_s≃kh S0/Δρ g =2π h/λ S0/Δρ g,

with sign depending on the sign convention for S0, usually quoted as e_s≃-kh S0/Δρ g.

The ρ↔Δρ identification is notational: the statement writes σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx, the geophysical buoyancy is Δρ g e. The exact free-base transfer with ρ is e_s=χ_ex S0/ρ g and with Δρ e_s=χ_ex S0/Δρ g.

Many colleagues quote the impermeable-base / lubrication normalisation W(h)=0, Φ(h)=0, which gives

χ_L(U)=U/[cosh U+U sinh U]=[sinh U+U⁻¹cosh U]⁻¹,  χ_L=U+O(U³),

the same thin-plate limit χ≃U and differing from χ_ex only at O(U³). The two forms are the source of the minor variant χ=kh/[cosh kh+kh sinh kh] versus χ=kh cosh kh/[ (kh)²+cosh² kh] appearing in the thread; they coincide to leading order and the viscosity-free long-wave scaling e_s∝S0/Δρ g with shape factor kh is unanimous.

Unresolved/notational points: sign convention for e_s vs S0, and whether the final reported χ is the exact free-base χ_ex or the commonly quoted lubrication χ_L. For the stated permeable base σ_zz(h)=0, w(h) free, the exact μ-independent transfer is χ_ex above, which reduces to χ≈kh in the thin-plate limit U≪1.

 =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}$,

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation is now fully converged on the rigid-lid biharmonic stream function with the steady kinematic lid

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Then $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ and with the buoyant restoring
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$ for the
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ basis $\Phi(z)=c z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-d k^{-1}z\sinh kz$.

With $U=kh$,

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
