2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The stream-function normal mode
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid impermeable lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in steady state.
On the lid $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ so that
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ and
$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_{s}/\mu$.

At the base the stated conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$,
$u_{z}(h)$ free. With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $C=-A$, $B+D=-2kA$,
and $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$.

Elimination of $A,B,D$ gives the $\mu$–free steady transfer

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh$,

i.e. on the buoyant normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0$, $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$, and the viscosity
drops out of the steady balance.

For the geophysically relevant long-wave thin-plate limit
$U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$,

$e_{s}\simeq U\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

the familiar viscosity independent dynamic-topography scaling.
With the conventional geophysical sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.

The lubrication / impermeable-base form
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]
 =[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U]^{-1}$,
is obtained if the extra kinematic condition $W(h)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$, is imposed at the base. It satisfies
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$
to $O(U)$; it is the $kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ form most often
quoted. The problem as stated imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not
$W(h)=0$, so the exact Stokes transfer for the stated conditions is
$\chi_{\rm ex}$ above, which reduces to the quoted thin-plate limit
$\chi\simeq kh$. On the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ normalisation used in
the statement $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with the same $\chi_{\rho}$.
No viscosity remains in the steady state.

7.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation has converged on a biharmonic stream-function solution with
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid no-slip lid: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$. On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ so
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ and $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$ for the
lid-admissible form $\Phi=c z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-dk^{-1}z\sinh kz$.

Base conditions used in the statement: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$u_z$ free.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.

This gives $(c+dh)\cosh kh=kc h\sinh kh$,
$d=c\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$ and
$2\mu c[ k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$, i.e.
$c=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\}$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_s =2\mu k c$ and
$e_s = S_{0}/(\Delta\rho g)\,\chi_A(U)$ with $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,
\[
\chi_A(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
       =\Big[\,U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\,\Big]^{-1}>0,
\]
viscosity independent in steady state.  Asymptotics:
$\chi_A=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_A\sim2U e^{-2U}$ for $U\gg1$.

Thin-plate long wave: $\cosh U\simeq1$,
$\chi_{LW}\simeq U=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $e_s\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
scaling with shape factor $kh$.  Sign is that of $S_{0}$; geophysical sign
convention often flips sign, $e_s\simeq -kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant used by several
colleagues gives the lubrication transfer
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+\cosh U/U]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_{L}\sim U\operatorname{sech}U$,
which coincides with $\chi_A$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin-plate
limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  All colleagues agree viscosity drops out of the
steady balance and $e_s\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Normalisation note: the statement writes $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ with
plate density $\rho$; the quoted form $e_s=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ uses the
buoyant density contrast $\Delta\rho$. The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
replacement is a trivial factor; with the statement's $\rho$,
$e_s=(S_{0}/\rho g)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$.

Unresolved nominal issue is only the $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ convention and
sign convention. The functional dependence $\chi(U)=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$,
and long-wave $\chi\approx kh$, is the stable consensus for the stated
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free-base problem.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The harmonic Stokes problem is settled in the group. With 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^2\Phi''+k^4\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Rigid free lid in steady state: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. 
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

Base conditions used in the statement are the permeable base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$,
no $w(h)=0$ imposed. Up to constants with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=Az\sinh kz+B[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz]$.
Then $B=\rho g e/2\mu k$ from the lid, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khA\cosh kh$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ gives
$S_0=2\mu k[A\cosh kh+khA\sinh kh+khB\cosh kh]$.
Eliminating $A,B$,

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$ with, up to the conventional
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification,

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}$,
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady balance. Long wave $U\ll1$,
$\cosh U\simeq1$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
the familiar thin-plate scaling $e_s\propto S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with shape
factor $kh$, $e_s\simeq 2\pi h/\lambda\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$U\to\infty$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0$.

If the density in the free-surface condition is kept as $\rho$, the strict
conversion to $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ carries $\rho/\Delta\rho$:
$\chi_{\rho/\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$;
with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the quoted form.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant is
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=U\sech U/[1+U\tanh U]$, which coincides
with the permeable-base $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$:
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$, $\chi_{L}\sim2U e^{-U}$ for $U\gg1$. This is the
lubrication form $\chi_L=U/(\cosh U+U\sinh U)$ often quoted in the literature.

Round 3 public responses: Colleagues 1–8 all recover the permeable-base exact
transfer $\chi_{\rm ex}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ with long-wave limit
$\chi\simeq U=kh$. All note viscosity independence and the $kh\ll1$ limit
$e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Sign conventions differ but magnitude is
identical. No substantive disagreement remains; remaining nuance is only the
$\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ normalisation and the permeable vs impermeable base
distinction, with the statement’s conditions corresponding to the permeable
base result above. Consensus is the $\mu$-free steady transfer and the
thin-plate limit $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The linear Stokes normal-mode is $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=- \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$. 
Rigid free lid in steady state: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. With buoyant restoring $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_s/\mu$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz e^{kz}+dz e^{-kz}$, $d=-2ka-b$ up to rigid motion, and
$P(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$, $b+d=-2ka$, $\rho g e_s=4\mu k^{2}a$ on the $\rho$ normalisation.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$,
$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_0$. With $U=kh$ this gives
$a k[\cosh U+U e^{-U}]+U b\cosh U=0$,
$a k[\cosh U-U e^{-U}]+b[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=S_0/4\mu k$,

$b=\dfrac{S_0}{4\mu k}\dfrac{\cosh U+U e^{-U}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}}$,
$a=-\dfrac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^{2}}\dfrac{S_0}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}}$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_s=4\mu k^{2}a$ is $\mu$-free:
$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,U\cosh U/[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U]$, $U=kh$,

$e_s=\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\left[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\right]^{-1}>0$,

$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$. With the $\rho$ normalisation used in the statement
$e_s=S_0/(\rho g)\,U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and the buoyant form is obtained by $\rho\to\Delta\rho$, i.e. an extra $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor if $\rho$ is kept distinct.

Asymptotics: $\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$. Long-wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

The often quoted impermeable-base / lubrication normalisation $W(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$ gives the equivalent transfer
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$, which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and yields the same thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$. All round-3 colleagues recover the $U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ exact free-base result and the $U/[ \cosh U+U\sinh U]$ lubrication form, with unanimous $\mu$-independence and the $kh$ long-wave scaling. Remaining trivial issues are the overall sign convention for $S_0$ and the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation of the restoring stress; sign is conventionally $e_s\simeq \mp kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

reflection_text.4:
The deliberation has converged on the steady Stokes transfer for a viscous sheet with a rigid impermeable lid u_x(0)=0 and a traction-free normal base σ_zz(h)=0, imposed basal shear σ_xz(h)=S0 sin kx and buoyant lid normal stress σ_zz(0)=Δρ g e cos kx. With stream function ψ=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ' sin kx, u_z=-kΦ cos kx, p=P(z) cos kx,
∇⁴ψ=0 → Φⁱᵛ-2k²Φ''+k⁴Φ=0, P=-μ k⁻¹[Φ'''-k²Φ'], σ_zz=μ k⁻¹[Φ'''-3k²Φ'] cos kx, σ_xz=μ[Φ''+k²Φ] sin kx.
Lid: Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 → σ_zz(0)=-P(0)=μ k⁻¹Φ'''(0)=Δρ g e_s.
Base: σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ'''(h)=3k²Φ'(h), σ_xz(h)=S0 ⇔ μ[Φ''(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S0.
With Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 the solution can be written Φ=A sinh kz+ B z sinh kz -A k z cosh kz etc. Elimination gives μ independent steady balance

Δρ g e_s = S0 U cosh U /[U²+cosh² U],  U=kh=2π h/λ,

i.e. on the conventional normalisation e_s=χ(U)S0/Δρ g

χ_ex(U)=U cosh U/[U²+cosh² U]=[U/ cosh U+cosh U/U]⁻¹>0,

so that the viscosity drops out of the steady state.  Asymptotic behaviour
χ_ex=U+O(U³) for U≪1, χ_ex∼2U e^{-2U}→0 for U≫1.  Hence the geophysically relevant thin-plate long-wave limit

χ_LW≃U=kh=2π h/λ,   e_s≃kh S0/Δρ g =2π h/λ S0/Δρ g,

with sign depending on the sign convention for S0, usually quoted as e_s≃-kh S0/Δρ g.

The ρ↔Δρ identification is notational: the statement writes σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx, the geophysical buoyancy is Δρ g e. The exact free-base transfer with ρ is e_s=χ_ex S0/ρ g and with Δρ e_s=χ_ex S0/Δρ g.

Many colleagues quote the impermeable-base / lubrication normalisation W(h)=0, Φ(h)=0, which gives

χ_L(U)=U/[cosh U+U sinh U]=[sinh U+U⁻¹cosh U]⁻¹,  χ_L=U+O(U³),

the same thin-plate limit χ≃U and differing from χ_ex only at O(U³). The two forms are the source of the minor variant χ=kh/[cosh kh+kh sinh kh] versus χ=kh cosh kh/[ (kh)²+cosh² kh] appearing in the thread; they coincide to leading order and the viscosity-free long-wave scaling e_s∝S0/Δρ g with shape factor kh is unanimous.

Unresolved/notational points: sign convention for e_s vs S0, and whether the final reported χ is the exact free-base χ_ex or the commonly quoted lubrication χ_L. For the stated permeable base σ_zz(h)=0, w(h) free, the exact μ-independent transfer is χ_ex above, which reduces to χ≈kh in the thin-plate limit U≪1.
reflection_text.3:
The steady Stokes stream-function solution is now stable across the round.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=-(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{zz}= -\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid free lid: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$.
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_s/\mu$.

Base as stated: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
No $W(h)=0$ condition is imposed.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$, elimination gives a $\mu$–independent steady balance

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}$,
$U=kh$,

i.e. on the conventional normalisation $e_s=\chi(U)S_0/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0$, $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady state. 
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\to0$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\to\infty$.

Long-wave thin-plate $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U\simeq1$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$,

$e_s\simeq U\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g
      =(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar $\mu$-independent viscous dynamic topography scaling. With the statement’s
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the formal factor is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm ex}S_0/\Delta\rho g$; with the usual identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ it is simply $\chi_{\rm ex}$ above.

The impermeable-base family $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ is often quoted as

$\chi_{L}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
 =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}$,

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 all converge to the exact
$U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ free-base transfer and the $U$ long-wave limit,
differences being only $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation and sign
convention $e_s\propto\pm S_0$. The sign is conventional; magnitude is as above.
Unresolved only the trivial $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor and sign convention.
reflection_text.8:
The deliberation is now fully converged on the rigid-lid biharmonic stream function with the steady kinematic lid

$\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid, impermeable lid in steady state: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\dot e=0$, $u_x(0)=0$.
Then $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ and with the buoyant restoring
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\Delta\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$ for the
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ basis $\Phi(z)=c z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-d k^{-1}z\sinh kz$.

Base conditions used in the statement: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$,
i.e. $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_0$.

With $U=kh$,

$(c+dh)\cosh U=kc h\sinh U$, $d=c[k\tanh U-1/h]$,

$2\mu[c hk^{2}\cosh U-d\cosh U-d hk\sinh U]=S_0$,

$c=S_0 h\cosh U/[2\mu\,(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)]$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k c=S_0\,U\cosh U/[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U]$ and

$e_s=\chi_{ex}(U)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
=\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}$, $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\mu$-independent in steady state. Long wave $U\ll1$: $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,
$\chi_{ex}=U+O(U^{3})$,

$e_s\simeq U S_0/\Delta\rho g =kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh$.

The $W(h)=0$ impermeable-base/lubrication family quoted by several colleagues is

$\chi_L(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U]^{-1}$,
and the $kW$ corrected form $\chi_7=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U+U^{2}/2]$.
$\chi_L$ and $\chi_{ex}$ coincide to $O(U)$ and share the same thin-plate limit
$\chi\simeq U$, the difference being $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ free base vs $W(h)=0$ 
impermeable base / $kW$ basal-shear treatment. All current colleagues 1-8 report
$\chi_{ex}$ as the exact free-base transfer and $\chi_L$ as the commonly quoted
lubrication form; long-wave behaviour is identical.

Sign is conventional: $e_s>0$ for $S_0>0$ up to the usual geophysical sign
$e_s\simeq -kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Density normalisation is $\rho\to\Delta\rho$;
with $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e$ the factor is $\chi_\rho=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$,
and $e_s=\chi_\rho S_0/\rho g$, which becomes $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ on
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.

The earlier round-0 dispute $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ vs $W'(0)=0$ only is resolved in favour
of the rigid lid $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ steady solution above. Unresolved nuance is only
the conventional $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor and sign convention; the physically
relevant thin-plate scaling is $e_s\approx kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with $\chi\simeq kh$.
∎
reflection_text.5:
The stream-function reduction is now unanimous across rounds 1-3. 
With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0\iff \Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Rigid impermeable lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives in steady state $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.
With buoyant restoring $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$ and viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

Base conditions stated: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_0$, no $W(h)=0$ imposed.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Cz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $A[u\sinh u-\cosh u]=Ch\cosh u$, $u=kh$, and the shear
condition gives $-2\mu kA[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]/[h\cosh u]=S_0$.
Eliminating $A,C$ with $\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}A$ :

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$,
i.e. $e_s=\chi_{\rm ex}(u)S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
 =\Big[\dfrac{u}{\cosh u}+\dfrac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}$,
$u=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\mu$-independent. 
$\chi_{\rm ex}=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\to0$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2u e^{-2u}\to0$ for $u\to\infty$.
Geophysically relevant thin-plate long wave $u\ll1$:

$\chi_{LW}\simeq u=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

The often quoted impermeable-base $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ lubrication normalisation is

$\chi_{L}(u)=\dfrac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
 =\big[\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u\big]^{-1}$,

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(u)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$\chi_{L}=u+O(u^{3})$. Colleagues 2,5,6,7,8 explicitly note this $W(h)=0$ variant;
colleague 7 notes the $u^{2}/2$ correction is the $O(kW)$ correction to the basal shear
condition. Sign is convention-dependent; magnitude is as above.

Density replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ is the
buoyant restoring stress used in the statement. Viscosity drops out, shape factor depends
only on $kh$, and the long-wave limit is $\chi\simeq kh$. This is the consensus in
round 3; no material change from round 2. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The stream-function normal mode
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx$,
$p=P(z)\cos kx$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid impermeable lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in steady state.
On the lid $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$ so that
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$ and
$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_{s}/\mu$.

At the base the stated conditions are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$,
$u_{z}(h)$ free. With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $C=-A$, $B+D=-2kA$,
and $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$.

Elimination of $A,B,D$ gives the $\mu$–free steady transfer

$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh$,

i.e. on the buoyant normalisation $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0$, $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$, and the viscosity
drops out of the steady balance.

For the geophysically relevant long-wave thin-plate limit
$U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$,

$e_{s}\simeq U\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =\dfrac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\dfrac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}$,

the familiar viscosity independent dynamic-topography scaling.
With the conventional geophysical sign $e_{s}\propto -S_{0}$.

The lubrication / impermeable-base form
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]
 =[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U]^{-1}$,
is obtained if the extra kinematic condition $W(h)=0$, i.e.
$\Phi(h)=0$, $u_{z}(h)=0$, is imposed at the base. It satisfies
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$
to $O(U)$; it is the $kh/[\cosh kh+kh\sinh kh]$ form most often
quoted. The problem as stated imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not
$W(h)=0$, so the exact Stokes transfer for the stated conditions is
$\chi_{\rm ex}$ above, which reduces to the quoted thin-plate limit
$\chi\simeq kh$. On the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ normalisation used in
the statement $e_{s}= \chi_{\rho}S_{0}/\rho g$ with the same $\chi_{\rho}$.
No viscosity remains in the steady state.
reflection_text.7:
The deliberation has converged on a biharmonic stream-function solution with
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= -[P+2\mu k\Phi']\cos kx =\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid no-slip lid: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$. On the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$ so
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s =\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$ and $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$ for the
lid-admissible form $\Phi=c z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-dk^{-1}z\sinh kz$.

Base conditions used in the statement: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$,
$u_z$ free.  $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff P(h)+2\mu k\Phi'(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.

This gives $(c+dh)\cosh kh=kc h\sinh kh$,
$d=c\big[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}\big]$ and
$2\mu c[ k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$, i.e.
$c=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\}$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_s =2\mu k c$ and
$e_s = S_{0}/(\Delta\rho g)\,\chi_A(U)$ with $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,
\[
\chi_A(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
       =\Big[\,U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\,\Big]^{-1}>0,
\]
viscosity independent in steady state.  Asymptotics:
$\chi_A=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_A\sim2U e^{-2U}$ for $U\gg1$.

Thin-plate long wave: $\cosh U\simeq1$,
$\chi_{LW}\simeq U=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, the familiar $e_s\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
scaling with shape factor $kh$.  Sign is that of $S_{0}$; geophysical sign
convention often flips sign, $e_s\simeq -kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant used by several
colleagues gives the lubrication transfer
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+\cosh U/U]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_{L}\sim U\operatorname{sech}U$,
which coincides with $\chi_A$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin-plate
limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  All colleagues agree viscosity drops out of the
steady balance and $e_s\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

Normalisation note: the statement writes $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$ with
plate density $\rho$; the quoted form $e_s=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ uses the
buoyant density contrast $\Delta\rho$. The $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$
replacement is a trivial factor; with the statement's $\rho$,
$e_s=(S_{0}/\rho g)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$.

Unresolved nominal issue is only the $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ convention and
sign convention. The functional dependence $\chi(U)=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$,
and long-wave $\chi\approx kh$, is the stable consensus for the stated
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free-base problem.
reflection_text.6:
The harmonic Stokes problem is settled in the group. With 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^2\Phi''+k^4\Phi=0$, 
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$, 
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Rigid free lid in steady state: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. 
$\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.

Base conditions used in the statement are the permeable base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx$,
no $w(h)=0$ imposed. Up to constants with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=Az\sinh kz+B[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz]$.
Then $B=\rho g e/2\mu k$ from the lid, $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives
$B[\cosh kh-kh\sinh kh]=khA\cosh kh$, and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$ gives
$S_0=2\mu k[A\cosh kh+khA\sinh kh+khB\cosh kh]$.
Eliminating $A,B$,

$\rho g e_s=S_0\,\dfrac{kh\cosh kh}{(kh)^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh}$,

i.e. with the buoyant restoring stress $\Delta\rho g e$,

$e_s=\chi(kh)\dfrac{S_0}{\Delta\rho g}$ with, up to the conventional
$\rho\to\Delta\rho$ identification,

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}$,
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady balance. Long wave $U\ll1$,
$\cosh U\simeq1$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
the familiar thin-plate scaling $e_s\propto S_0/\Delta\rho g$ with shape
factor $kh$, $e_s\simeq 2\pi h/\lambda\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
$U\to\infty$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0$.

If the density in the free-surface condition is kept as $\rho$, the strict
conversion to $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$ carries $\rho/\Delta\rho$:
$\chi_{\rho/\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$;
with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is the quoted form.

The $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ impermeable-base variant is
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=U\sech U/[1+U\tanh U]$, which coincides
with the permeable-base $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$:
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$, $\chi_{L}\sim2U e^{-U}$ for $U\gg1$. This is the
lubrication form $\chi_L=U/(\cosh U+U\sinh U)$ often quoted in the literature.

Round 3 public responses: Colleagues 1–8 all recover the permeable-base exact
transfer $\chi_{\rm ex}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ with long-wave limit
$\chi\simeq U=kh$. All note viscosity independence and the $kh\ll1$ limit
$e_s\approx kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Sign conventions differ but magnitude is
identical. No substantive disagreement remains; remaining nuance is only the
$\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ normalisation and the permeable vs impermeable base
distinction, with the statement’s conditions corresponding to the permeable
base result above. Consensus is the $\mu$-free steady transfer and the
thin-plate limit $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$. ∎
reflection_text.1:
The linear Stokes normal-mode is $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$, $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=- \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$. 
Rigid free lid in steady state: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$ and $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$. With buoyant restoring $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_s/\mu$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz e^{kz}+dz e^{-kz}$, $d=-2ka-b$ up to rigid motion, and
$P(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$, $b+d=-2ka$, $\rho g e_s=4\mu k^{2}a$ on the $\rho$ normalisation.

Base: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$,
$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_0$. With $U=kh$ this gives
$a k[\cosh U+U e^{-U}]+U b\cosh U=0$,
$a k[\cosh U-U e^{-U}]+b[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=S_0/4\mu k$,

$b=\dfrac{S_0}{4\mu k}\dfrac{\cosh U+U e^{-U}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}}$,
$a=-\dfrac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^{2}}\dfrac{S_0}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}}$.

Hence $\Delta\rho g e_s=4\mu k^{2}a$ is $\mu$-free:
$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,U\cosh U/[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U]$, $U=kh$,

$e_s=\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$, 
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\left[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\right]^{-1}>0$,

$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$. With the $\rho$ normalisation used in the statement
$e_s=S_0/(\rho g)\,U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and the buoyant form is obtained by $\rho\to\Delta\rho$, i.e. an extra $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor if $\rho$ is kept distinct.

Asymptotics: $\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$ and $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\gg1$. Long-wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

The often quoted impermeable-base / lubrication normalisation $W(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$ gives the equivalent transfer
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$, which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and yields the same thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$. All round-3 colleagues recover the $U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ exact free-base result and the $U/[ \cosh U+U\sinh U]$ lubrication form, with unanimous $\mu$-independence and the $kh$ long-wave scaling. Remaining trivial issues are the overall sign convention for $S_0$ and the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation of the restoring stress; sign is conventionally $e_s\simeq \mp kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.

2.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx  .
$$

In the steady state the rigid lid is

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
$$

and with the buoyant restoring stress

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx
$$

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s} .
\tag{1}
$$

On the permeable base

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

$u_{z}(h)$ being free.  With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=\big(A+Bz\big)e^{kz}+\big(C+Dz\big)e^{-kz},\qquad
C=-A,\;B+D=-2kA,
$$

so that $\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A .
\tag{2}
$$

Eliminating $A,B,D$ from $\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$ with $U=kh$ gives

$$
S_{0}=2\mu kA\,\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{U\cosh U},
$$

and with (2)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh .
$$

Hence on the buoyant normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the viscosity drops out of the steady balance.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\;U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0,\;U\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$,
$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$ and

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

i.e. to leading order $\chi\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$, the familiar
$\mu$–independent viscous dynamic topography scaling.  With the
conventional geophysical sign $\sigma_{xz}(h)=-S_{0}$ this is
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

In the often quoted impermeable-base lubrication normalisation
$W(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$, this is written as

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin
plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  Up to the trivial $\rho\leftrightarrow
\Delta\rho$ replacement this is the usual $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\rho g$
dynamic-topography law. ∎

4.text:
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ put

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

so that with $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

The rigid free lid is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
          =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that $\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}/\mu$.
Up to rigid motion, with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(z)=A\sinh kz+Bz\sinh kz-Akz\cosh kz ,
$$

and

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A ,\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=4\mu k^{2}A .
\tag{2}
$$

The permeable base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .
$$

With $U=kh$ the two base conditions give

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
      =2\mu kA\,\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{U\cosh U}=S_{0},
\tag{3}
$$

so that on eliminating $A$ between (2) and (3) the viscosity drops out
of the steady balance,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. with the conventional normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\tag{4}
$$

which is $\mu$ independent.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\;U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0,\;U\to\infty .
$$

With the $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation the transfer is
usually quoted in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1},
\qquad \chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with (4) to $O(U)$.  For the geophysically relevant
long wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

so that to leading order

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
     =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
     =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law.
With the usual geophysical sign convention $\sigma_{xz}(h)=-S_{0}$ this
is $e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  On the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the
same $\chi_{\rm ex}$ is obtained with $\rho$ in place of $\Delta\rho$,
$ e_{s}= \chi_{\rm ex}S_{0}/\rho g$, i.e. $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi_{\rm ex}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  This is the $\mu$ free steady Stokes
transfer for $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$; the often quoted
lubrication value $\chi\simeq kh$ is the $U\ll1$ limit of (4). ∎

3.text:
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ put on the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\;u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\;p=P(z)\cos kx,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ i.e.

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the rigid free lid $u_{x}(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyant restoring condition $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,
e\cos kx$

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s} .
\tag{1}
$$

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz},\qquad C=-A,
\qquad D=-B-2kA,
$$

so that on the lid
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A$ and (1) is
$\Delta\rho g e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A$.
The free-base conditions used in the statement are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

$u_{z}(h)$ free.  With $U=kh$ elimination of $A,B,D$ gives the
$\mu$–free steady transfer

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. on the conventional buoyant normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/
\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
     =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
 \qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

so that with the $\rho$  normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$
quoted in the statement

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
       \frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}\,
       \frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

and for the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the viscosity
drops out of the steady balance.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\;U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0,\;U\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$,
$\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$ and

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar $\mu$–independent viscous dynamic topography scaling.
Up to sign, $e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ in the usual
geophysical sign convention.  With the often quoted impermeable base
normalisation $W(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$,

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin
plate long wave limit $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.  This is the
$\chi\simeq kh$ viscous topographic transfer, $|\chi|\approx kh$,
viscosity independent in the steady state, the sign being that of
$S_{0}$. ∎

5.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

On the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$ in the steady state

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyant restoring stress $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s} ,
\tag{1}
$$

and $\dot e=0$.  Up to rigid motion

$$
\Phi(z)=A\big[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz\big]+Cz\sinh kz,
$$

so that $\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$ and

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=-2\mu k^{2}A .
\tag{2}
$$

The dynamic base conditions stated in the problem are the free normal
stress and the prescribed shear,

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

with $u_{z}(h)$ free.  Putting $u=kh$ the normal stress free condition
gives $A\big[u\sinh u-\cosh u\big]=Ch\cosh u$ and

$$
-2\mu kA\,\frac{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}{h\cosh u}=S_{0},
\tag{3}
$$

whence with (2)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u},\qquad u=kh,
$$

i.e. on the normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(u)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=\frac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
   =\Big[\,\frac{u}{\cosh u}+\frac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad u=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

which is $\mu$ independent in the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\qquad u\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)\sim2u\,e^{-2u}\to0,\qquad u\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $u=kh\ll1$,
$\cosh u=1+O(u^{2})$,

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=u+O(u^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq u\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}=kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

i.e. up to the conventional sign

$$
\chi_{LW}=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},\qquad
e_{s}\simeq kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law.
With the usual geophysical sign convention $\sigma_{xz}(h)=-S_{0}$ this is
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  With the often quoted
impermeable base normalisation $W(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$ the lubrication
form

$$
\chi_{L}(u)=\frac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
          =\Big[\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u\Big]^{-1}=u+O(u^{3}),
$$

coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(u)$ and gives the same thin plate
limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  The replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho ge\cos kx$ is the buoyant restoring stress used in
the statement.  The viscosity drops out of the steady balance and the
shape factor depends only on $kh$. ∎

8.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$,

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=-\big[P+2\mu k\Phi'\big]\cos kx
       =\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx  .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$ the rigid free lid is

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0,\qquad u_{x}(0)=0,
$$

so that on the lid $\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyant restoring traction

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx
$$

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s}.
\tag{1}
$$

Up to rigid motion with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-
d k^{-1}z\sinh kz ,
$$

$$
P(z)=2\mu\big[-kc\cosh kz+d\sinh kz\big].
$$

The permeable base conditions used in the statement are

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

so that with $U=kh$

$$
\big(c+dh\big)\cosh U=kc h\sinh U,\qquad 
d=c\Big[k\tanh U-\frac1h\Big],
$$

and

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
      =2\mu c\,\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{h\cosh U}=S_{0}.
$$

Hence

$$
c=\frac{S_{0}h\cosh U}{2\mu\big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big]},\qquad
\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c .
$$

From (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=2\mu k c
   =S_{0}\,\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

i.e. on the buoyant normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
   =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
 $$

which is $\mu$ independent in the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant long wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$,

$$
\cosh U=1+O(U^{2}),\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

so that to leading order

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography scaling.
With the conventional impermeable base $W(h)=\Phi(h)=0$ normalisation this
is usually quoted in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin
plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$.  Up to the usual geophysical sign
$e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. $|e_{s}|\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
the viscosity drops out of the steady balance and the shape factor is
$kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.  With $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the same
expression is $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm ex}S_{0}/\rho g$, i.e.
$e_{s}=\chi_{\rm ex}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ on the identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.  This is the quoted $e_{s}\propto S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
dynamic topography law.

6.text:
With the normal mode

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ is $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$ and

\begin{equation*}
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\bigl[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\bigr],\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\bigl[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\bigr]\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\bigl[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\bigr]\sin kx ,
\end{equation*}
so that on the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

In the steady state $\dot e=0$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e_{s}\cos kx=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx ,
\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\rho g}{\mu}e_{s} ,
\tag{1}
$$

and with the permeable base used in the statement

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\bigl[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\bigr]=S_{0}.
\tag{2}
$$

Up to rigid motion $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ gives

$$
\Phi(z)=Az\sinh kz+B\Big[z\cosh kz-k^{-1}\sinh kz\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=2\mu kB\cos kx
      =\rho g e_{s}\cos kx,
\qquad 
B=\frac{\rho g e_{s}}{2\mu k},
$$

and (2) with $U=kh$ gives

$$
B\bigl[\cosh U-U\sinh U\bigr]=UA\cosh U ,\qquad
S_{0}=2\mu k\Big[A\cosh U+UA\sinh U+UB\cosh U\Big] .
$$

Eliminating $A,B$ the viscosity drops out of the steady balance and

$$
\rho g e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\tag{3}
$$

i.e. on the buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \chi_{\rm ex}(U)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0 .
$$

In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad U\to0,\qquad
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0,\qquad U\to\infty,
$$

so that for the geophysically relevant long–wave thin plate
$U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
 $$

the familiar $\mu$–independent viscous dynamic topography law.  
With the sign convention $\sigma_{xz}(h)=-S_{0}$ this is $e_{s}\simeq
-kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  Keeping the $\rho$ appearing in 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ distinct from the buoyant $\Delta\rho$,

$$
e_{s}= \frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}\,
\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

so that on the $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ normalisation

$$
\chi_{\rho/\Delta}(U)=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
\;\;\xrightarrow[U\ll1]{}\;\;
\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,U
=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,kh
=\frac{\rho}{\Delta\rho}\,\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

and with the usual identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$,
$\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.  On the conventional
$W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation this is quoted in the
lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
      =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
thin-plate limit $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$, i.e. the
$\mu$-free steady viscous topographic transfer with shape factor $kh$.
Up to sign this is $e_{s}\approx \pm kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$\chi\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$. ∎

1.text:
In the normal mode

$$
\psi=\Phi (z)\sin kx ,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{z}=-k\Phi \cos kx ,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\Big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\Big] ,
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}\Big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\Big]\cos kx ,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}= \mu\Big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\Big]\sin kx .
$$

On the rigid lid $u_{x}(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0 ,\qquad 
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx .
$$

With the buoyant restoring traction 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e\cos kx$ in the steady state
$\dot e=0$

$$
\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g\,e_{s},\qquad 
\Phi'''(0)=\frac{k\Delta\rho g}{\mu}e_{s}, \tag{1}
$$

and with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$

$$
\Phi(z)=a\sinh kz+bz e^{kz}+dz e^{-kz},\qquad d=-2ka-b .
$$

The permeable, normal stress free base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0},
$$

i.e. with $U=kh$

$$
ak\Big[\cosh U+U e^{-U}\Big]+U b\cosh U=0,
$$
$$
ak\Big[\cosh U-Ue^{-U}\Big]+b\Big[\cosh U+U\sinh U\Big]
     =\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k}\; .
$$

Hence

$$
b=\frac{S_{0}}{4\mu k}
\frac{\cosh U+Ue^{-U}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}},\qquad
a=-\frac{U\cosh U}{4\mu k^{2}}
   \frac{S_{0}}{\cosh^{2}U+U^{2}} ,
$$

and $P(0)=-2\mu k(b+d)$, $b+d=-2ka$.  From (1)

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=4\mu k^{2}a
   =S_{0}\,\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad 
   U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

so that on the conventional buoyant normalisation

$$
e_{s}=\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},\qquad
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
     =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
$$

which is $\mu$ independent in the steady state.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\;U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0,\;U\to\infty .
$$

For the geophysically relevant thin-plate long wave limit
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$ and

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\qquad 
e_{s}\simeq U\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =kh\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

i.e. up to the conventional sign $e_{s}\simeq\mp kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law.
With the usual $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation the transfer is
written in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
thin-plate limit $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.  On the $\rho$
normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ used in the statement
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ so that with the
buoyant form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$
is carried over, $\chi_{\rho/\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/
\big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big]\to(\rho/\Delta\rho)U$ for $U\ll1$, i.e.
$e_{s}\simeq(\rho/\Delta\rho)kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with the sign that of $S_{0}$.  In the usual geophysical identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$|\chi|\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$, the viscosity dropping out of the
steady balance.  With the opposite sign convention $e_{s}\simeq
 -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

$W(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$, this is written as

          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin

public_text.4:
In the steady state $\dot e=0$ put

$$
\psi(x,z)=\Phi(z)\sin kx,\qquad 
u_{x}=\Phi'\sin kx,\qquad u_{z}=-k\Phi\cos kx,\qquad 
p=P(z)\cos kx ,
$$

so that with $\nabla^{4}\psi=0$

$$
\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0 ,\qquad 
P=-\frac{\mu}{k}\big[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi'\big],
$$

$$
\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}\big[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi'\big]\cos kx,\qquad
\sigma_{xz}=\mu\big[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi\big]\sin kx .
$$

The rigid free lid is
$\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_{x}(0)=0$, and

$$
\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\frac{\mu}{k}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx
          =\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}\cos kx ,
\tag{1}
$$

so that $\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}/\mu$.
Up to rigid motion, with $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$,

$$
\Phi(z)=A\sinh kz+Bz\sinh kz-Akz\cosh kz ,
$$

and

$$
\Phi'''(0)=-4k^{3}A ,\qquad 
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=4\mu k^{2}A .
\tag{2}
$$

The permeable base is

$$
\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff \Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h),\qquad
\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff 
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]=S_{0} .
$$

With $U=kh$ the two base conditions give

$$
\mu\big[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)\big]
      =2\mu kA\,\frac{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}{U\cosh U}=S_{0},
\tag{3}
$$

so that on eliminating $A$ between (2) and (3) the viscosity drops out
of the steady balance,

$$
\Delta\rho g\,e_{s}=S_{0}\,
\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U},\qquad U=kh,
$$

i.e. with the conventional normalisation $e_{s}=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\frac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\frac{U}{\cosh U}+\frac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0,
\qquad U=kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
\tag{4}
$$

which is $\mu$ independent.  In particular

$$
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),\;U\to0,\qquad 
\chi_{\rm ex}(U)\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0,\;U\to\infty .
$$

With the $W(h)=0$ impermeable base normalisation the transfer is
usually quoted in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1},
\qquad \chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with (4) to $O(U)$.  For the geophysically relevant
long wave thin plate $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U=1+O(U^{2})$,

$$
\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

so that to leading order

$$
e_{s}\simeq U\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
     =kh\,\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
     =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
\qquad 
\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda},
$$

the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law.
With the usual geophysical sign convention $\sigma_{xz}(h)=-S_{0}$ this
is $e_{s}\simeq -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  On the $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$
normalisation used in the statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the
same $\chi_{\rm ex}$ is obtained with $\rho$ in place of $\Delta\rho$,
$ e_{s}= \chi_{\rm ex}S_{0}/\rho g$, i.e. $e_{s}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)
\chi_{\rm ex}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.  This is the $\mu$ free steady Stokes
transfer for $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$; the often quoted
lubrication value $\chi\simeq kh$ is the $U\ll1$ limit of (4). ∎

      =kh\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g}
      =\frac{2\pi h}{\lambda}\frac{S_{0}}{\Delta\rho g},
$$

i.e. up to the conventional sign $e_{s}\simeq\mp kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
the familiar viscosity independent viscous dynamic topography law.

written in the lubrication form

$$
\chi_{L}(U)=\frac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
          =\Big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\Big]^{-1}=U+O(U^{3}),
$$

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same
thin-plate limit $\chi_{LW}\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.  On the $\rho$
normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ used in the statement
$e_{s}=S_{0}/\rho g\;U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ so that with the
buoyant form $e_{s}=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ the factor $\rho/\Delta\rho$
is carried over, $\chi_{\rho/\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/
\big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big]\to(\rho/\Delta\rho)U$ for $U\ll1$, i.e.
$e_{s}\simeq(\rho/\Delta\rho)kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$
with the sign that of $S_{0}$.  In the usual geophysical identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is $e_{s}\approx kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,
$|\chi|\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$, the viscosity dropping out of the
steady balance.  With the opposite sign convention $e_{s}\simeq
 -kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$. ∎

sign is conventional $e_{s}\propto\pm S_{0}$. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The normal-mode Stokes problem is now settled in the group. With
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^4\psi=0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^2\Phi''+k^4\Phi=0$ and
$P=- \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^2\Phi']$,

$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^2\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^2\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid impermeable lid $u_x(0)=0$ is $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ in steady state.
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With the buoyant restoring traction $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_s$, $\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_s/\mu$.

Base conditions as stated are
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$,
$u_z(h)$ free. With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$
$\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$, $C=-A$, $B+D=-2kA$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-4k^3A$ and $\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^2A$.

Elimination of $A,B,D$ from $\Phi'''(h)=3k^2\Phi'(h)$ and
$\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^2\Phi(h)]=S_0$ with $U=kh$ gives the $\mu$-free steady
transfer

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_0\,U\cosh U/\bigl[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\bigr]$,

i.e. on the buoyant normalisation $e_s=\chi_{\rm ex}(U)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
      =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0$,
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$
for $U\gg1$, viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

For the geophysically relevant long-wave thin-plate limit $U=kh\ll1$, 
$\cosh U=1+O(U^2)$,

$\chi_{LW}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$, $e_s\simeq U S_0/\Delta\rho g
=kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=2\pi h/\lambda\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar viscosity-independent dynamic-topography scaling, sign
convention $e_s\propto -S_0$ in the usual geophysical sign.

The lubrication/impermeable-base form most often quoted,

$\chi_L(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
       =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}=U+O(U^3)$,

is obtained if the extra kinematic condition $W(h)=0$, i.e. $\Phi(h)=0$,
$u_z(h)=0$, is imposed at the base. It coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to
$O(U)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$.
The problem as stated imposes only $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, not $W(h)=0$, so
the exact Stokes transfer for the stated conditions is $\chi_{\rm ex}$
above, which reduces to the quoted thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$.

On the $\rho$ normalisation used in the statement
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$, $e_s=S_0/\rho g\;U\cosh U/(U^2+\cosh^2U)$,
so that with the buoyant form $e_s=\chi S_0/\Delta\rho g$
$\chi_{\rho/\Delta}=(\rho/\Delta\rho)U\cosh U/(U^2+\cosh^2U)\to
(\rho/\Delta\rho)U$ for $U\ll1$. With the conventional identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ this is $e_s\approx kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
$|\chi|\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$, viscosity independent in steady state.
Sign is that of $S_0$; conventional geophysical sign gives $e_s\simeq
-kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$. Unresolved notational $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ factor
remains a trivial rescaling.

reflection_text.1:
The steady Stokes normal mode is 
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=- \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Rigid free lid: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$, 
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With buoyant restoring $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)=\Delta\rho g e_s$, $\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_s/\mu$.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ the permeable normal-stress-free base
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ together with
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_0$, $\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_0$ gives, with
$U=kh$,

$\Delta\rho g e_s = S_0\, U\cosh U\big/\big[U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U\big]$,
i.e. on the buoyant normalisation $e_s=\chi_{\rm ex}(U)S_0/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0$, 
$U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\mu$-free in steady state. Asymptotics
$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2U e^{-2U}\to0$
for $U\gg1$. Long-wave thin plate $U\ll1$,
$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_0/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_0/\Delta\rho g$,
viscosity drops out.

The often quoted impermeable-base / lubrication normalisation
$W(h)=0$, $\Phi(h)=0$ gives the equivalent transfer

$\chi_{L}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
 =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}=U+O(U^{3})$,

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and yields the same
thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$. Round 4 colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,7,8 all
recover $\chi_{\rm ex}=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and the $U\ll1$
limit $\chi\simeq kh$, with unanimous $\mu$-independence. 

Remaining trivial issues are overall sign convention $e_s\approx\mp kh
S_0/\Delta\rho g$ and the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation
of the restoring stress. With the $\rho$ normalisation used in the
statement $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ one gets
$e_s=S_0/\rho g\,U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and the buoyant form is
obtained by $\rho\to\Delta\rho$, i.e. an extra $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor
if $\rho$ is kept distinct. With the conventional identification
$\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ the stable magnitude is $|\chi|\simeq kh=
2\pi h/\lambda$ in the long-wave limit, $|\chi|=
U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ exactly for the free-base Stokes sheet,
and $|\chi|=U/(\cosh U+U\sinh U)$ in the lubrication/impermeable-base
form most often quoted.
reflection_text.5:
The stream-function reduction is now stable across rounds 1-4.

With $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0\iff \Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$,
$P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid impermeable lid $u_x(0)=0$ gives in steady state $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$ and
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$.
With buoyant restoring $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e/\mu$ and viscosity drops out of the steady balance.

Base conditions as stated: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$ and
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$, no $W(h)=0$ imposed.
With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi(z)=A[\sinh kz-kz\cosh kz]+Cz\sinh kz$,
$\Phi'''(0)=-2Ak^{3}$.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$ gives $A[u\sinh u-\cosh u]=Ch\cosh u$, $u=kh$, and the shear
condition gives $-2\mu kA[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]/[h\cosh u]=S_{0}$.
Eliminating $A,C$ with $\Delta\rho g e_s=-2\mu k^{2}A$ :

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,u\cosh u/[u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u]$,
i.e. $e_s=\chi_{\rm ex}(u)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ with

$\chi_{\rm ex}(u)=\dfrac{u\cosh u}{u^{2}+\cosh^{2}u}
 =\Big[\dfrac{u}{\cosh u}+\dfrac{\cosh u}{u}\Big]^{-1}$,
$u=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\mu$-independent. 
$\chi_{\rm ex}=u+O(u^{3})$ for $u\to0$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2u e^{-2u}\to0$ for $u\to\infty$.
Geophysically relevant thin-plate long wave $u\ll1$:

$\chi_{LW}\simeq u=kh$, $e_s\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The often quoted impermeable-base $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ lubrication normalisation is

$\chi_{L}(u)=\dfrac{u}{\cosh u+u\sinh u}
 =\big[\sinh u+u^{-1}\cosh u\big]^{-1}$,

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(u)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit
$\chi_{L}=u+O(u^{3})$. Colleagues 2,5,6,7,8 explicitly note this $W(h)=0$ variant;
colleague 7 notes the $u^{2}/2$ correction is the $O(kW)$ correction to the basal shear
condition. Sign is convention-dependent; magnitude is as above.

Density replacement $\rho\to\Delta\rho$ in $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ is the
buoyant restoring stress used in the statement. Viscosity drops out, shape factor depends
only on $kh$, and the long-wave limit is $\chi\simeq kh$. This is the consensus in
rounds 1-4; round 4 shows unanimity on $\chi_{\rm ex}$ with the thin-plate $kh$ limit, no
material change from round 3. ∎
reflection_text.7:
The discussion has converged on the biharmonic stream-function normal mode
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$
with $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}=\mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, $\sigma_{xz}=\mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.
Rigid no-slip lid: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi'(0)=0$ so $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.
With buoyant normalisation $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,
$\Delta\rho g e_s=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)$, $\Phi'''(0)=2k^{2}c$ for the lid-admissible form
$\Phi=c\,z\cosh kz-c k^{-1}\sinh kz-dk^{-1}z\sinh kz$.

Base conditions in the statement: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$, $u_z$ free.
$\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
This gives $(c+dh)\cosh kh=kch\sinh kh$, $d=c[k\tanh kh-h^{-1}]$ and
$2\mu c[ k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]/[h\cosh kh]=S_{0}$,
$c=S_{0}h\cosh kh/\{2\mu[k^{2}h^{2}+\cosh^{2}kh]\}$.
Hence $\Delta\rho g e_s=2\mu k c$ and
$e_s=S_{0}/(\Delta\rho g)\,\chi_{\rm ex}(U)$ with $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
   =\Big[\,U/\cosh U+\cosh U/U\,\Big]^{-1}>0$,

viscosity independent in steady state. Asymptotics:
$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\ll1$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2U e^{-2U}$ for $U\gg1$.
Thin-plate long wave: $\cosh U\simeq1$, $\chi_{LW}\simeq U=kh$,
$e_s\simeq kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.
Sign is that of $S_{0}$; geophysical sign convention is often $e_s\simeq -kh S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$.

The impermeable-base variant $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ used by several earlier colleagues gives the lubrication transfer
$\chi_{L}(U)=U/[\cosh U+U\sinh U]=[\sinh U+\cosh U/U]^{-1}$,
$\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$, $\chi_{L}\sim U\operatorname{sech}U$,
which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit $\chi\simeq kh$.
All colleagues in round 4 now quote $\chi_{\rm ex}$ as the exact permeable-base solution and note $\chi_{L}$ as the common lubrication/impermeable normalisation.

Normalisation note: statement writes $\sigma_{zz}=\rho g e\cos kx$; the quoted form $e_s=\chi S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$ uses buoyant density contrast $\Delta\rho$. With the statement's $\rho$, $e_s=(S_{0}/\rho g)U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$; the $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ replacement is a trivial factor, usually identified $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$.

Unresolved nominal issues remain only sign convention and the $\rho$ vs $\Delta\rho$ bookkeeping. Functional dependence $\chi(U)=U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and long-wave $\chi\approx kh$ is the stable consensus for the stated $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0$, $\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}$ free-base problem, viscosity drops out of the steady balance.
reflection_text.4:
The deliberation has now converged on the μ-free steady Stokes transfer for a rigid lid u_x(0)=0, w(0)=ė, σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx, σ_zz(h)=0, σ_xz(h)=S0 sin kx.

With ψ=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ′ sin kx, u_z=−kΦ cos kx, p=P(z) cos kx,
∇⁴ψ=0 → Φⁱᵛ−2k²Φ″+k⁴Φ=0,
P=−μk⁻¹[Φ‴−k²Φ′], 
σ_zz=μ k⁻¹[Φ‴−3k²Φ′] cos kx,
σ_xz=μ[Φ″+k²Φ] sin kx.

Lid: Φ(0)=Φ′(0)=0, σ_zz(0)=μ k⁻¹Φ‴(0)=ρ g e_s.
Base: σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ‴(h)=3k²Φ′(h), σ_xz(h)=S0 ⇔ μ[Φ″(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S0.

With Φ(0)=Φ′(0)=0 the μ-independent steady balance is

Δρ g e_s = S0 U cosh U /[U²+cosh² U],   U=kh=2π h/λ,

i.e. on the buoyant normalisation e_s=χ_ex(U) S0/Δρ g with

χ_ex(U)=U cosh U/[U²+cosh² U]=[U/ cosh U+ cosh U/U]⁻¹>0.

Asymptotics χ_ex=U+O(U³) for U≪1, χ_ex∼2U e^{−2U}→0 for U≫1.
Hence the geophysically relevant thin-plate long-wave limit

χ_LW≃U=kh=2π h/λ,    e_s≃ kh S0/Δρ g =2π h/λ S0/Δρ g,

viscosity drops out. Sign is conventional: with σ_xz(h)=+S0 the
quoting is e_s≃+kh S0/Δρ g, geophysical sign convention gives e_s≃−kh
S0/Δρ g.

The statement writes σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx. On that ρ normalisation
e_s=χ_ex S0/ρ g. With the buoyant form σ_zz=Δρ g e the factor is
 carried over as e_s=(ρ/Δρ)χ_ex S0/Δρ g, normally identified ρ≡Δρ.

A minority lubrication/impermeable base normalisation W(h)=0, Φ(h)=0
gives the frequently quoted

χ_L(U)=U/[cosh U+U sinh U]=[sinh U+U⁻¹cosh U]⁻¹=U+O(U³),

which coincides with χ_ex to O(U) and has the same thin-plate limit
χ≈U. The two forms are the source of the minor variant
U cosh U/(U²+cosh²U) versus U/(cosh U+U sinh U) seen in the thread;
they are indistinguishable for kh≪1.

No new contradictions appear in round 4. All colleagues 1-8 reproduce the
same μ-free transfer, the same long-wave scaling e_s∝S0/Δρ g with shape
factor kh, and note the ρ↔Δρ and sign conventions. Unresolved notational
points remain: sign of S0 vs e_s, and whether the final reported χ is
the exact free-base χ_ex or the commonly quoted lubrication χ_L. For the
stated permeable base σ_zz(h)=0, w(h) free, the exact μ-independent
transfer is χ_ex above, reducing to χ≈kh in the thin-plate limit.
reflection_text.8:
The round-4 public set is now essentially unanimous on the rigid-lid biharmonic
stream-function solution in steady state. With the normal mode

ψ=Φ(z) sin kx, u_x=Φ' sin kx, u_z=−kΦ cos kx, p=P(z) cos kx,
∇⁴ψ=0 ⇔ Φⁱᵛ−2k²Φ''+k⁴Φ=0,
P=−μk⁻¹[Φ'''−k²Φ'],

σ_zz= μk⁻¹[Φ'''−3k²Φ'] cos kx, σ_xz= μ[Φ''+k²Φ] sin kx.

Rigid, impermeable lid in steady state: Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0, ḟe=0,
σ_zz(0)=−P(0)= μk⁻¹Φ'''(0) cos kx. With the buoyant restoring
σ_zz(0)=Δρ g e cos kx one has μk⁻¹Φ'''(0)=Δρ g e_s, Φ'''(0)=kΔρ g e_s/μ.

Free normal base, prescribed shear, u_z free:

σ_zz(h)=0 ⇔ Φ'''(h)=3k²Φ'(h),  σ_xz(h)=S₀ sin kx ⇔
μ[Φ''(h)+k²Φ(h)]=S₀.

With Φ(0)=Φ'(0)=0 the basis can be taken as
Φ(z)=c z cosh kz−c k⁻¹sinh kz−d k⁻¹z sinh kz,
Φ'''(0)=2k²c, σ_zz(0)=2μkc cos kx.
Base conditions give (U=kh)

(c+dh) coshU = k c h sinhU, d=c[ k tanhU −1/h],
2μ[ c h k² coshU −d coshU − d h k sinhU]=S₀,

hence c= S₀ h coshU/[2μ(U²+cosh²U)] and

Δρ g e_s =2μk c = S₀ U coshU/[U²+cosh²U].

Hence on the buoyant normalisation

e_s = χ_ex(U) S₀/Δρ g,
χ_ex(U)= U coshU/[U²+cosh²U]=[U/ coshU+ coshU/U]⁻¹,
U=kh=2π h/λ,

μ–independent in the steady balance.  Long wave U≪1:
coshU=1+O(U²), χ_ex=U+O(U³),

e_s ≃ U S₀/Δρ g = kh S₀/Δρ g =2πh/λ S₀/Δρ g,
χ_LW ≃ kh.

The W(h)=0 impermeable-base/lubrication family quoted in R0 is
χ_L(U)=U/[coshU+U sinhU]=[sinhU+U⁻¹coshU]⁻¹,
and the kW corrected form χ_7=U/[coshU+U sinhU+U²/2].
χ_L and χ_ex coincide to O(U) and share the thin-plate limit χ≃U;
the difference is σ_zz(h)=0 free base vs W(h)=0 impermeable base/kW
basal-shear treatment. The round-4 colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 all give
χ_ex as the exact free-base transfer and χ_L as the commonly quoted
lubrication form.

Sign and density normalisation remain conventional. With the statement
σ_zz(0)=ρ g e cos kx the ρ–normalised factor is
χ_ρ(U)=U coshU/[U²+cosh²U] and e_s=χ_ρ S₀/ρ g.  On the requested
e_s=χ S₀/Δρ g this is χ=(ρ/Δρ)χ_ρ, and with the usual geophysical
identification ρ≡Δρ one writes simply χ_ex.  The geophysical sign
convention is e_s≃−kh S₀/Δρ g for positive basal shear; the magnitude is
|χ|≃kh.

Unresolved nuance is only the conventional ρ/Δρ factor and sign; the
physically relevant thin-plate scaling is e_s≈kh S₀/Δρ g with
χ≈kh=2πh/λ, viscosity dropping out of the steady state. ∎
reflection_text.3:
The steady Stokes stream-function solution is now stable across rounds.

With normal mode $\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,

$\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=-(\mu/k)[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$,
$\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$, 
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid free lid: $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $u_x(0)=0$.
$\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)=(\mu/k)\Phi'''(0)\cos kx$.

With the buoyant normalisation used for the final scaling $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\Delta\rho g e\cos kx$,

$\Phi'''(0)=k\Delta\rho g e_s/\mu$.

Base as stated: $\sigma_{zz}(h)=0\iff\Phi'''(h)=3k^{2}\Phi'(h)$,
$\sigma_{xz}(h)=S_{0}\sin kx\iff\mu[\Phi''(h)+k^{2}\Phi(h)]=S_{0}$.
No $W(h)=0$ impermeable condition is imposed; $u_z(h)$ is free.

With $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\Phi(z)=(A+Bz)e^{kz}+(C+Dz)e^{-kz}$,
$C=-A$, $D=-B-2kA$, elimination gives a $\mu$-independent steady balance

$\Delta\rho g e_s=S_{0}\,\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}$,
$U=kh$,

i.e. on the conventional normalisation $e_s=\chi(U)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$

$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=\dfrac{U\cosh U}{U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U}
 =\Big[\dfrac{U}{\cosh U}+\dfrac{\cosh U}{U}\Big]^{-1}>0$, $U=kh=2\pi h/\lambda$.

Viscosity drops out of the steady state. 
$\chi_{\rm ex}(U)=U+O(U^{3})$ for $U\to0$, $\chi_{\rm ex}\sim2Ue^{-2U}\to0$ for $U\to\infty$.

Long-wave thin-plate $U=kh\ll1$, $\cosh U\simeq1$,

$\chi_{\rm ex}=U+O(U^{3})$,

$e_s\simeq U\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g=kh\,S_{0}/\Delta\rho g
      =(2\pi h/\lambda)S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$,

the familiar $\mu$-independent viscous dynamic topography scaling.

With the statement’s top condition $\sigma_{zz}(0)=\rho g e\cos kx$ the formal factor is
$e_s=(\rho/\Delta\rho)\chi_{\rm ex}S_{0}/\Delta\rho g$; with the usual geophysical identification $\rho\equiv\Delta\rho$ it is simply $\chi_{\rm ex}$ above.

The impermeable-base family $W(h)=0\iff\Phi(h)=0$ often quoted in the literature is

$\chi_{L}(U)=\dfrac{U}{\cosh U+U\sinh U}
 =\big[\sinh U+U^{-1}\cosh U\big]^{-1}$,

which coincides with $\chi_{\rm ex}$ to $O(U)$ and gives the same thin-plate limit $\chi_{L}=U+O(U^{3})$. Colleagues 1-8 all converge to the exact free-base transfer $U\cosh U/(U^{2}+\cosh^{2}U)$ and the $U$ long-wave limit, differences being only $\rho\leftrightarrow\Delta\rho$ normalisation and sign convention $e_s\propto\pm S_0$. Sign is conventional; magnitude is as above. Unresolved only the trivial $\rho/\Delta\rho$ factor and sign convention; the physically quoted thin-plate result is $|\chi|\simeq kh=2\pi h/\lambda$, i.e. $e_s\simeq \pm kh S_0/\Delta\rho g$.
reflection_text.6:
The harmonic Stokes problem is now settled in round 4. With normal mode
$\psi=\Phi(z)\sin kx$, $u_x=\Phi'\sin kx$, $u_z=-k\Phi\cos kx$, $p=P(z)\cos kx$,
$\nabla^{4}\psi=0$ gives $\Phi^{iv}-2k^{2}\Phi''+k^{4}\Phi=0$, $P=-\mu k^{-1}
[\Phi'''-k^{2}\Phi']$, $\sigma_{zz}= \mu k^{-1}[\Phi'''-3k^{2}\Phi']\cos kx$,
$\sigma_{xz}= \mu[\Phi''+k^{2}\Phi]\sin kx$.

Rigid free lid $u_x(0)=0$ : $\Phi(0)=\Phi'(0)=0$, $\sigma_{zz}(0)=-P(0)
=\mu k^{-1}\Phi'''(0)\cos kx =\rho g e\cos kx$, i.e. $\Phi'''(0)=k\rho g e/\mu$.
